title: حِكَايَةُ الْخَيَّاطِ
titleEn: The Tailor's Tale, continued: the Barber's Tale of Himself and His First Brother
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 247–258 (Night 31, continuing directly from nights-30), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 31 opens at the judge's door, where the barber tells the judge that the young man is his master and shouts that the household has beaten him; the judge sends him in. The young man, telling his own story, describes hiding in a chest, being carried off by the barber, breaking his leg in the fall, scattering gold on the crowd, and fleeing through Baghdad with the barber at his heels, until he leaves the city. The barber then boasts of his silence before the company, telling how he once joined ten robbers in a boat and was brought before the Caliph al-Mustanṣir, and then begins the tale of his six brothers with the first, the hunchback tailor, whom a lady and her husband make a fool of in the mill; the second brother, Baqbāt the paralytic, is lured by an old woman into a house where he is slapped, shaved and stripped. The night ends mid-scene as Shahrazad falls silent; the final word is damaged in print and left as printed. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some of the Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْحَادِيَةُ وَالثَّلٰثُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānat al-laylatu al-ḥādiyatu wa-al-thalāthūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the first-and-thirtieth.
sentences.i: And when the thirty-first night came,
sentences.n: The night-opening formula. The print writes الثلثون without the alif of ثلاثون, so it is pointed with a dagger alif (ٰ) to read thalāthūn. الحادية is the feminine of "first" used for the units in compound ordinals: "the one-and-thirtieth".

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِى أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الْقَاضِيَ قَالَ لِلْغِلْمَانِ مَا الَّذِي فَعَلَهُ سَيِّدُكُمْ حَتَّى أَقْتُلَهُ وَهَذِهِ دَارِي بَيْنَ أَيْدِيكُمْ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-qāḍiya qāla li-al-ghilmāni mā al-ladhī faʿalahu sayyidukum ḥattā aqtulahu wa-hādhihi dārī bayna aydīkum
sentences.l: She said: It-reached me, O king the-fortunate, that the judge said to the lads: What (is) that-which he-did, your master, that I-kill him; and this (is) my house, between your hands?
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the judge said to the servants, "What has your master done that I should kill him? And this is my own house, right here before you!"
sentences.n: Shahrazād takes up the tale. The judge answers the barber's charge (end of the last night) that he has been beating the young man. بَيْنَ أَيْدِيكُمْ, "between your hands", means "in front of you, under your eyes"; the lads are the young man's servants who have come with the barber.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْمُزَيِّنُ أَنْتَ ضَرَبْتَهُ فِى هَذِهِ السَّاعَةِ بِالْمَقَارِعِ وَأَنَا أَسْمَعُ عِيَاطَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-muzayyinu anta ḍarabtahu fī hādhihi al-sāʿati bi-al-maqāriʿi wa-anā asmaʿu ʿiyāṭahu
sentences.l: And said to-him the barber: You, you-struck-him in this hour with the whips, and I, I-hear his shouting.
sentences.i: The barber replied, "You beat him this very hour with whips; I could hear his screams!"
sentences.n: ضَرَبْتَهُ, "you struck him", is said of the judge who gave the order (so also below). الْمَقَارِعِ are whips or scourges (singular مِقْرَعَة). عِيَاط is "shouting, crying out", a word of the spoken language.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْقَاضِي وَمَا الَّذِي فَعَلَهُ حَتَّى أَقْتُلَهُ وَمَنْ أَدْخَلَهُ دَارِي وَمِنْ أَيْنَ إِلَى أَيْنَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-qāḍī wa-mā al-ladhī faʿalahu ḥattā aqtulahu wa-man adkhalahu dārī wa-min ayna ilā ayna
sentences.l: And said the judge: And what (is) that-which he-did, that I-kill him? and who made-him-enter my house? and from where, to where?
sentences.i: The judge said, "And what has he done that I should kill him? Who let him into my house? Where has he come from, and where is he bound?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْمُزَيِّنُ لَاتَكُنْ شَيْخًا نَحْسًا وَأَنَا أَعْلَمُ الْحِكَايَةَ وَالْحَالُ كُلُّهُ بِنْتُكَ تَعْشَقُهُ وَهُوَ يَعْشَقُهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-muzayyinu lā-takun shaykhan naḥsan wa-anā aʿlamu al-ḥikāyata wa-al-ḥālu kulluhu bintuka taʿshaquhu wa-huwa yaʿshaquhā
sentences.l: And said to-him the barber: Do-not-be an old-man ill-omened, and I, I-know the tale; and the state, all-of-it: your-daughter loves-him and he loves-her.
sentences.i: The barber said to him, "Don't play the unlucky old man. I know the whole story: your daughter is in love with him and he is in love with her."
sentences.n: لَاتَكُنْ is printed as one word. نَحْس is "ill-omened, unlucky". The construction وَالْحَالُ كُلُّهُ بِنْتُكَ تَعْشَقُهُ is loose ("the situation, all of it: your daughter loves him"), the sort of juxtaposition Middle Arabic prefers to a subordinate clause. عَشِقَ is passionate, bodily love.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّهُ قَدْ دَخَلَ دَارَكَ أَمَرْتَ غِلْمَانَكَ فَضَرَبُوهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ʿalimta annahu qad dakhala dāraka amarta ghilmānaka fa-ḍarabūhu
sentences.l: And when you-knew that-he had entered your-house, you-ordered your-lads, and they-struck-him.
sentences.i: "When you learned that he had come into your house, you ordered your servants, and they beat him."

sentences.t: وَاللَّهِ مَا بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكَ إِلَّا الْخَلِيفَةُ أَوْ تُخْرِجَ لَنَا سَيِّدَنَا يَأْخُذُهُ أَهْلُهُ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ أَدْخُلَ وَأُخْرِجَهُ مِنْ عِنْدِكُمْ وَتَخْجَلَ أَنْتَ
sentences.tr: wa-Allāhi mā baynanā wa-baynaka illā al-khalīfatu aw tukhrija lanā sayyidanā yaʾkhudhuhu ahluhu min qabli an adkhula wa-ukhrijahu min ʿindikum wa-takhjala anta
sentences.l: And-by-God, there is-not between-us and between-you except the caliph, or you bring-out to-us our-master, (that) take-him his-family, before that I-enter and I-bring-him-out from with-you, and you-be-shamed, you.
sentences.i: "By God, nothing lies between us and you but the Caliph, unless you bring our master out to us for his family to take, before I go in and fetch him out of your house and you are put to shame."
sentences.n: أَوْ تُخْرِجَ: after أَوْ in the sense "unless" the verb is subjunctive, as here. يَأْخُذُهُ أَهْلُهُ stays indicative, as a loosely attached clause ("his family taking him"). The final وَتَخْجَلَ keeps the subjunctive of أَنْ أَدْخُلَ: "before I enter, bring him out, and you are shamed".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْقَاضِي وَقَدِ الْتَجَمَ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ وَتَغْتَمُّ بِالْحَيَاءِ مِنَ النَّاسِ إِنْ كُنْتَ صَادِقًا فَادْخُلْ أَنْتَ وَأَخْرِجْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-qāḍī wa-qadi iltajama ʿani al-kalāmi wa-taghtammu bi-al-ḥayāʾi mina al-nāsi in kunta ṣādiqan fa-adkhul anta wa-akhrijhu
sentences.l: And said to-him the judge, and he had been-bridled from speech, and (is) grieved with shame before the people: If you-are truthful, then enter, you, and bring-him-out.
sentences.i: The judge, struck dumb as if bridled and wretched with shame before the onlookers, said to him, "If you are telling the truth, go in yourself and bring him out."
sentences.n: اِلْتَجَمَ (a passive-sense form of لَجَمَ, "to bridle") is "to be reined in, left speechless". وَتَغْتَمُّ is pointed as printed, an imperfect with the prefix ت, which fits poorly after the perfect الْتَجَمَ; it may be a misprint for وَاغْتَمَّ ("and was grieved"). I translate the sense, not the tense.

sentences.t: فَهَمَزَ الْمُزَيِّنُ وَدَخَلَ الدَّارَ
sentences.tr: fa-hamaza al-muzayyinu wa-dakhala al-dāra
sentences.l: And spurred (himself) the barber, and entered the house.
sentences.i: At that the barber sprang forward and went into the house.
sentences.n: هَمَزَ is "to prod, goad", as one pricks a mount with the heel; used alone like this it must mean "he bounded forward". I infer that sense from the verb's root meaning; I cannot confirm it from the lexicons for this intransitive use.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَيْتُ الْمُزَيِّنَ دَخَلَ طَلَبْتُ طَرِيقًا لِلْخُرُوجِ وَالْهُرُوبِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾaytu al-muzayyina dakhala ṭalabtu ṭarīqan li-al-khurūji wa-al-hurūbi
sentences.l: And when I saw the barber (had) entered, I sought a way for the going-out and the fleeing.
sentences.i: When I saw that the barber had gone in, I looked for a way to get out and escape.
sentences.n: The young man is speaking again, telling the caliph how he hid from the barber in the judge's house.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ أَجِدْدُونَ أَنِّي رَأَيْتُ فِي الطَّبَقَةِ الَّتِي أَنَا فِيهَا صُنْدُوقًا كَبِيرًا فَدَخَلْتُ فِيهِ وَرَدَيْتُ الْغِطَاءَ عَلَيَّ وَقَطَعْتُ نَفَسِي
sentences.tr: fa-lam ajiddūna annī raʾaytu fī al-ṭabaqati allatī anā fīhā ṣundūqan kabīran fa-dakhaltu fīhi wa-radaytu al-ghiṭāʾa ʿalayya wa-qaṭaʿtu nafasī
sentences.l: And I did not find, short-of (it), that I saw, in the storey which I (was) in, a chest big; and I entered in-it, and I turned-back the lid upon me, and I cut my breath.
sentences.i: I could think of nothing, until I saw in the upper room where I was a large chest. I climbed into it, pulled the lid down over me, and held my breath.
sentences.n: اجددون is two words run together in the print, أَجِدْ دُونَ; it is kept as one token and pointed as such. I read لَمْ أَجِدْ دُونَ أَنِّي رَأَيْتُ as "I found nothing [else to do] short of [the fact] that I saw..."; the sense is clear, the exact grammar is not. وَرَدَيْتُ is Middle Arabic for رَدَدْتُ: the doubled verb has been inflected like a weak one (as with حَسِيتُ earlier). قَطَعَ نَفَسَهُ is the idiom "to hold one's breath".

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَ الْقَاعَةَ فَلَمْ يَدْ خُلْهَا إِلَّا أَنْ رَجَعَ عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhala al-qāʿata fa-lam yad khulhā illā an rajaʿa ʿalayya
sentences.l: And he entered the hall, and he did-not enter-it except that he came-back at me.
sentences.i: He came into the hall, and no sooner was he inside than he turned back toward me.
sentences.n: يد خلها is one word split by a stray space in the print (يَدْخُلْهَا, jussive after لَمْ); the two halves are kept apart as printed. لَمْ يَدْخُلْهَا إِلَّا أَنْ means "he had barely entered it when".

sentences.t: وَاطَّلَعَ عَلَى الْمَوْضِعِ الَّذِي أَنَا فِيــهِ وَالْتَفَتَ يَمِينًا وَشِمَالًا
sentences.tr: wa-iṭṭalaʿa ʿalā al-mawḍiʿi al-ladhī anā fīhi wa-iltafata yamīnan wa-shimālan
sentences.l: And he looked-over upon the place which I (was) in, and turned right and left.
sentences.i: He peered at the spot where I was, and looked to the right and to the left,
sentences.n: The print stretches فيه with a tatweel (فيــه); it carries no meaning.

sentences.t: وَتَقَدَّمَ لِلصُّنْدُوقِ الَّذِي أَنَا فِيهِ وَحَمَلَهُ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ فَغَابَ رُشْدِي ثُمَّ مَرَّ مُسْرِعًا
sentences.tr: wa-taqaddama li-al-ṣundūqi al-ladhī anā fīhi wa-ḥamalahu ʿalā raʾsihi fa-ghāba rushdī thumma marra musriʿan
sentences.l: And he advanced to the chest which I (was) in, and carried-it upon his head, and my right-mind went-absent; then he passed, hurrying.
sentences.i: Then he walked up to the chest I was in and hoisted it onto his head. My wits deserted me. Then he strode off in haste.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا عَلِمْتُ أَنَّهُ مَا يَتْرُكُنِي جَذَبْتُ نَفْسِي وَفَتَحْتُ الصُّنْدُوقَ وَرَمَيْتُ نَفْسِي إِى أَرْضٍ فَانْكَسَرَتْ رِجْلِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ʿalimtu annahu mā yatrukunī jadhabtu nafsī wa-fataḥtu al-ṣundūqa wa-ramaytu nafsī ilā arḍin fa-inkasarat rijlī
sentences.l: And when I knew that-he (was) not leaving-me, I pulled my-self, and I opened the chest, and I threw my-self to a ground, and my-leg broke.
sentences.i: When I understood that he would never let me go, I pulled myself together, threw open the chest, and flung myself to the ground; and my leg broke.
sentences.n: اى is the print's spelling; the word is surely إِلَى with the lām dropped (a misprint), and it is pointed and read as ilā. This is how the young man came by his lame leg.

sentences.t: وَانْفَتَحَ الْبَابُ فَشَاهَدْتُ عَلَى الْبَابِ خَلْقًا كَثِيرًا
sentences.tr: wa-infataḥa al-bābu fa-shāhadtu ʿalā al-bābi khalqan kathīran
sentences.l: And the door opened, and I beheld at the door creatures many.
sentences.i: The door burst open, and at the door I saw a great crowd.
sentences.n: خَلْق, "creation, creatures", is the stock word for a crowd of people. The text does not say how the door came open.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ فِي كُمِّي ذَهَبًا كَثِيرًا أَعْدَدْتُهُ لِمِثْلِ هَذَا الْيَوْمِ وَمِثْلِ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna fī kummī dhahaban kathīran aʿdadtuhu li-mithli hādhā al-yawmi wa-mithli hādhā al-amri
sentences.l: And there-was in my-sleeve gold (acc.) much (acc.), I-had-prepared-it for the like of this day and the like of this affair.
sentences.i: In my sleeve I had a great deal of gold, which I had put by for just such a day and just such an emergency.
sentences.n: ذَهَبًا كَثِيرًا is accusative after كَانَ where Classical Arabic would have the nominative (ذَهَبٌ كَثِيرٌ): a very common Middle Arabic feature, kept as printed. The sleeve served as a pocket.

sentences.t: فَجَعَلْتُ أَنْثُرُ الذَّهَبَ عَلَى النَّاسِ لِيَشْتَغِلُوا بِهِ فَأَخَذُوهُ وَاشْتَغَلُوا بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-jaʿaltu anthuru al-dhahaba ʿalā al-nāsi li-yashtaghilū bihi fa-akhadhūhu wa-ishtaghalū bihi
sentences.l: And I began scattering the gold upon the people, that they be-occupied with-it; and they took-it and were-occupied with-it.
sentences.i: I began to scatter the gold over the people to keep them busy, and they snatched it up and were busy with it.

sentences.t: وَصِرْتُ أَجْرِي فِي أَزِقَّةِ بَغْدَادَ يَمِينًا وَشِمَالًا
sentences.tr: wa-ṣirtu ajrī fī aziqqati Baghdāda yamīnan wa-shimālan
sentences.l: And I became running in the lanes of Baghdad, right and left,
sentences.i: Then I ran through the alleys of Baghdad, to the right and to the left,

sentences.t: وَهَذَا الْمُزَيِّنُ الْمَلْعُونُ خَلْفِي وَأَيُّ مَكَانٍ دَخَلْتُ فِيهِ يَدْخُلُ هَذَا الْمُزَيِّنُ خَلْفِى
sentences.tr: wa-hādhā al-muzayyinu al-malʿūnu khalfī wa-ayyu makānin dakhaltu fīhi yadkhulu hādhā al-muzayyinu khalfī
sentences.l: and this barber, the cursed, behind me; and whatever place I-entered in-it, enters this barber behind me,
sentences.i: with that accursed barber at my heels; and into whatever place I went, he came in after me,
sentences.n: وَهَذَا الْمُزَيِّنُ ... خَلْفِي has no verb: "and this barber (was) behind me". The second خلفى is printed with ى, the first with ي; both are the same word.

sentences.t: وَهُوَ يَقُولُ أَرَادُوا يُفَجِّعُونِي فِي سَيِّدِي الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي نَصَرَنِي عَلَيْهِمْ وَخَلَّصَ سَيِّدِي مِنْ أَيْدِيهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-huwa yaqūlu arādū yufajjiʿūnī fī sayyidī al-ḥamdu li-Allāhi al-ladhī naṣaranī ʿalayhim wa-khallaṣa sayyidī min aydīhim
sentences.l: and he saying: They-wanted they-bereave-me in my-master. The-praise (is) for God who gave-me-victory over-them and delivered my-master from their hands.
sentences.i: all the while crying, "They meant to rob me of my master! Praise be to God, who gave me victory over them and delivered my master from their hands!"
sentences.n: أَرَادُوا يُفَجِّعُونِي has no أَنْ between the two verbs ("they wanted they would bereave me"), a regular Middle Arabic pattern. فَجَّعَ بِـ is "to afflict someone with the loss of" something; here "bereave me of my master". The barber's "victory" is of course the beating the young man took.

sentences.t: فَمَا زِلْتُ يَسُؤُنِي تَدْبِيرُكَ حَتَّى فَعَلْتَ بِنَفْسِكَ هَذِهِ الْفِعَالَ
sentences.tr: fa-mā ziltu yasuʾunī tadbīruka ḥattā faʿalta bi-nafsika hādhihi al-fiʿāla
sentences.l: And I did-not cease — it-grieves-me, your-management — until you-did to your-self these deeds.
sentences.i: I never stopped, though your scheming grieved me, until you brought all this on yourself.
sentences.n: The print has يسوني with no hamza sign; I point it يَسُؤُنِي, the verb "it grieves me" (Classical يَسُوءُنِي). The clause is loosely strung: "I did not cease — your management grieves me — until...". تَدْبِير is planning, management, scheming; الْفِعَال is used as a plural of "deeds".

sentences.t: فَلَوْلَا مَنُّ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ بِي مَا كُنْتَ خَلَصْتَ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْمُصِيبَةِ الَّتِي وَقَعْتَ فِيهَا وَكَانُوا يَرْمُونَكَ فِي مُصِيبَةٍ لَا تَخْلُصُ أَبَدًا
sentences.tr: fa-lawlā mannu Allāhi ʿalayka bī mā kunta khalaṣta min hādhihi al-muṣībati allatī waqaʿta fīhā wa-kānū yarmūnaka fī muṣībatin lā takhluṣu abadan
sentences.l: And had-it-not-been-for the favour of God upon you through me, you would-not-have escaped from this calamity which you fell in-it; and they were casting-you into a calamity you-do-not-escape ever.
sentences.i: Had God not shown you favour through me, you would never have escaped the calamity you fell into; and they were about to cast you into one you could never escape.
sentences.n: The print puts a shadda on the nun of منّ; it is the noun مَنّ, "favour, kindness" (from مَنَّ عَلَى), here in construct with اللَّه. بِي says that God's favour came by means of the speaker. مُصِيبَةٍ لَا تَخْلُصُ has no relative pronoun ("a calamity you do not escape"), which Arabic allows after an indefinite noun.

sentences.t: ؤَكَمْ تُرِيدُ أَنَا أَعِيشُ لَكَ حَتَّى أُخَلِّصَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-kam turīdu anā aʿīshu laka ḥattā ukhalliṣaka
sentences.l: And how-much do-you-want, I live for-you until I deliver-you?
sentences.i: And how long do you expect me to go on living for your sake, until I have saved you?
sentences.n: The print has ؤكم, with a waw-with-hamza where وكم is meant; it is a misprint, kept as printed. تُرِيدُ أَنَا أَعِيشُ again has no أَنْ ("you want I live").

sentences.t: وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ أَهْلَكْتَنِي بِسُوءِ تَدْبِيرِكَ وَكُنْتَ تُرِيدُ أَنَّكَ تَرُوحُ وَحْدَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-Allāhi laqad ahlaktanī bi-sūʾi tadbīrika wa-kunta turīdu annaka tarūḥu waḥdaka
sentences.l: By-God, you-have indeed destroyed-me by the badness of your-management; and you-were wanting that-you go alone.
sentences.i: By God, you have ruined me with your wretched scheming! You wanted to go off on your own.
sentences.n: أَنَّكَ تَرُوحُ, "that you go", where Classical Arabic would have أَنْ تَرُوحَ: a finite clause (أَنَّ plus indicative) takes the place of the subjunctive, a Middle Arabic habit.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ مَا نُوأَخِذُكَ عَلَى جَهْلِكَ لِأَنَّكَ قَلِيلُ الْعَقْلِ عَجُولٌ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin mā nuʾākhidhuka ʿalā jahlika li-annaka qalīlu al-ʿaqli ʿajūlun
sentences.l: But we-do-not-hold-you-to-account for your-ignorance, because-you (are) scant of the reason, hasty.
sentences.i: But I do not hold your folly against you, for you are short of sense and rash.
sentences.n: نوأخذك is the print's spelling of نُؤَاخِذُكَ (muʾākhadha, "to take someone to task, hold him to account"), with the alif of the long vowel unwritten; I point it نُوأَخِذُكَ and read it nuʾākhidhuka. The "we" is the barber speaking of himself. قَلِيلُ الْعَقْلِ, "scant of reason", is a construct adjective.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ مَا كَفَاكَ مَا جَرَى مِنْكَ حَتَّى تَجْرِيَ وَرَآيَ وَتَتَكَلَّمَ مَعِي بِمِثْلِ هَذَا الْكَلَامِ فِى الْأَسْوَاقِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu mā kafāka mā jarā minka ḥattā tajriya warāya wa-tatakallama maʿī bi-mithli hādhā al-kalāmi fī al-aswāqi
sentences.l: And I said to-him: Did it not suffice you, what happened from you, until you run behind-me and speak with-me with the like of this speech in the markets?
sentences.i: I said to him, "Was it not enough, what you have already done, that you must run behind me and talk to me like this in the marketplaces?"
sentences.n: وَرَآيَ: the print's spelling of وَرَائِي ("behind me"), with a madda alif; I read it warāya, as the colloquial form has it. مَا كَفَاكَ is a rhetorical question: "was it not enough for you?"

sentences.t: وَكَادَتْ رُوحِي تَذْهَقُ مِنِّي مِنْ شِدَّةِ غَيْظِي مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: wa-kādat rūḥī tadhhaqu minnī min shiddati ghayẓī minhu
sentences.l: And my-spirit nearly went-out from me from the intensity of my-rage at-him.
sentences.i: My very soul was ready to leave me, so fierce was my rage at him.
sentences.n: تَذْهَقُ is printed with ذ; the usual verb for a soul "departing" is زَهَقَتْ (zahaqat), and ذهق may be a variant or a slip of the print. The sense is the same.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلْتُ دُكَّانًا فِي وَسَطِ السُّوقِ وَاسْتَجَرْتُ بِالْحَائِكِ فَمَنَعَهُ عَنِّي
sentences.tr: fa-dakhaltu dukkānan fī wasaṭi al-sūqi wa-istajartu bi-al-ḥāʾiki fa-manaʿahu ʿannī
sentences.l: And I entered a shop in the middle of the market, and I sought-protection with the weaver, and he kept-him from me.
sentences.i: I went into a shop in the middle of the market and begged the weaver for his protection, and he kept the barber away from me.
sentences.n: اِسْتَجَارَ بِـ means "to seek the protection of" someone; the weaver is evidently the shop's owner. The young man is still speaking, telling how he tried to shake off the barber.

sentences.t: وَجَلَسْتُ فِي مَخْزَنٍ وَقُلْتُ فِي نَفْسِي مَا عُلْتُ أَقْدِرُ أَفْتَرِقُ مِنْ هَذَا الْمُزَيِّنِ الْمَلْعُونِ وَهُوَ يُقِيمُ عِنْدِي لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا
sentences.tr: wa-jalastu fī makhzanin wa-qultu fī nafsī mā ʿultu aqdiru aftariqu min hādhā al-muzayyini al-malʿūni wa-huwa yuqīmu ʿindī laylan wa-nahāran
sentences.l: And I sat in a storeroom, and I said in my self: I no-longer (ʿultu) am-able, I part from this barber, the accursed, while he stays with me night and day.
sentences.i: I sat down in a storeroom and said to myself, "I can no longer get free of this accursed barber, who stays beside me night and day."
sentences.n: مَا عُلْتُ is printed with a lām, but the sense wants مَا عُدْتُ, "I no longer ..." (the dāl and lām are easily confused in this print); the word is pointed as the letters stand, and the translation follows the sense. أَقْدِرُ أَفْتَرِقُ, "I am able, I part", has no linking أَنْ: two verbs set side by side, a Middle Arabic habit that recurs below (أَحْضَرْتُ, سَكَنْتُ, أَتَكَلَّمُ). افترق من means "to part from".

sentences.t: وَلَا بَقِيَ فِّي رَمَقٌ أَنْظُرُ إِلَى خَلْقَتِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-lā baqiya fiyya ramaqun anẓuru ilā khalqatihi
sentences.l: And there did not remain in-me a breath (of life); I look at his make-up.
sentences.i: and I had not a breath of strength left in me to look upon his face.
sentences.n: The print puts a shadda on the fāʾ of فّي; it plainly belongs on the yā' (فِيَّ, "in me"), and it is kept where printed. رَمَق is the last bit of life or strength left in a person. خَلْقَة, "make, build", is used here for his whole appearance.

sentences.t: فَأَرْسَلْتُ فِي الْوَقْتِ أَحْضَرْتُ الشُّهُودَ وَكَتَبْتُ وَصِيَّةً لِأَهْلِي وَفَرَّقْتُ مَالِي
sentences.tr: fa-arsaltu fī al-waqti aḥḍartu al-shuhūda wa-katabtu waṣiyyatan li-ahlī wa-farraqtu mālī
sentences.l: And I sent in the time, I-had-present the witnesses, and I wrote a testament for my family, and I distributed my wealth.
sentences.i: At once I sent for the witnesses and had them brought, and I wrote out a will for my family and divided up my property.
sentences.n: فَأَرْسَلْتُ أَحْضَرْتُ puts "I sent" and "I had present" side by side with no conjunction; it means "I sent and brought". فِي الْوَقْتِ, "in the time", is "at once".

sentences.t: وَعَمِلْتُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَاظِرًا وَأَمَرْتُهُ أَنْ يَبِيعَ الدَّارَ وَالْعَقَارَاتِ وَوَصَّيْتُهُ بِالْكِبَارِ وَالصِّغَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿamiltu ʿalayhim nāẓiran wa-amartuhu an yabīʿa al-dāra wa-al-ʿaqārāti wa-waṣṣaytuhu bi-al-kibāri wa-al-ṣighāri
sentences.l: And I made over them an overseer, and I commanded him that he sell the house and the landed-properties, and I charged him with the great-ones and the small-ones.
sentences.i: I appointed a steward over them, ordered him to sell the house and the estates, and entrusted the elders and the little ones to his care.
sentences.n: عَمِلَ عَلَيْهِمْ نَاظِرًا, "to make an overseer over them": ʿamila is used in the sense of "appoint". The "them" are his household. الْكِبَار وَالصِّغَار, "the big and the small", can mean the old and the young of the family, or the larger and smaller matters of the estate; the pointing leaves both open. وَصَّى بِـ means "to charge someone with, to commend something to".

sentences.t: وَخَرَجْتُ مُسَافِرًا مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْوَقْتِ حَتَّى أَتَخَلَّصَ مِنْ هَذَا الْقَوَّادِ وَجِئْتُ سَكَنْتُ فِي بَلَدِكُمْ وَلِي فِيهَا مُدَّةٌ
sentences.tr: wa-kharajtu musāfiran min dhālika al-waqti ḥattā atakhallaṣa min hādhā al-qawwādi wa-jiʾtu sakantu fī baladikum wa-lī fīhā muddatun
sentences.l: And I went-out travelling from that time, until I be-delivered from this pimp; and I came (and) I-dwelt in your town, and to-me in it (is) a while.
sentences.i: That same hour I set out as a traveller, so as to be rid of this pimp; and I came and settled in your town, where I have now lived for some time.
sentences.n: قَوَّاد is a pimp, a procurer: the young man's word for the barber, used frankly. وَجِئْتُ سَكَنْتُ joins "I came" and "I dwelt" with no link, as before. وَلِي فِيهَا مُدَّةٌ, "and to me in it a while", means "and I have been there for a while"; the "it" is the town.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا عَزَمْتُمْ عَلَيَّ فَهَا أَنَا جِئْتُ لَكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ʿazamtum ʿalayya fa-hā anā jiʾtu lakum
sentences.l: And when you resolved upon me, then here I (am), I came to you.
sentences.i: So when you pressed me to come, here I am: I have come to you.
sentences.n: عَزَمَ عَلَى is "to insist upon" someone, the way a host presses a guest to accept an invitation. The print marks the shadda on عليّ, so the shadda is kept. The "then" (فَ) before هَا أَنَا opens the main clause after فَلَمَّا.

sentences.t: فَرَأَيْتُ هَذَا الْمَلْعُونَ الْقَوَّادَ عِنْدَكُمْ فِي صَدْرِ الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-raʾaytu hādhā al-malʿūna al-qawwāda ʿindakum fī ṣadri al-makāni
sentences.l: And I saw this accursed one, the pimp, with you in the chest of the place.
sentences.i: and there I saw this accursed pimp among you, in the seat of honour.
sentences.n: صَدْرُ الْمَكَانِ, "the chest of the place", is the place of honour at the head of the room.

sentences.t: فَكَيْفَ يَطِيبُ قَلْبِي وَمَقَامِي عِنْدَكُمْ مَعَ هَذَا وَقَدْ فَعَلَ بِي هَذِهِ الْفِعَالَ
sentences.tr: fa-kayfa yaṭību qalbī wa-maqāmī ʿindakum maʿa hādhā wa-qad faʿala bī hādhihi al-fiʿāla
sentences.l: So how shall my heart be-good, and my staying with you together-with this one, when he has done to me these deeds?
sentences.i: How can my heart be at ease, or my stay with you, in the company of this man, after what he has done to me?
sentences.n: هَذِهِ الْفِعَالَ: فِعَال is a plural of فِعْل, "deed", here treated as feminine singular like a collective (the print has no alif, الْأَفْعَال, which would be the usual plural). طَابَ قَلْبُهُ, "his heart was good", means to be at ease, content.

sentences.t: وَانْكَسَرَتْ رِجْلِي بِسَبَبِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-inkasarat rijlī bi-sababihi
sentences.l: And my leg was broken by the cause of him.
sentences.i: and my leg was broken because of him.
sentences.n: The lame young man's grievance in a few words: this is the reason he limps.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الشَّابَّ امْتَنَعَ مِنَ الْجُلُوسِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-shābba imtanaʿa mina al-julūsi
sentences.l: Then indeed the young man refused from sitting.
sentences.i: Then the young man refused to sit down.
sentences.n: The narrating voice changes here. The words so far were the lame young man's, speaking to the company; now the Tailor is again reporting to the caliph, and "we" are the guests at that feast.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْنَا حِكَايَتَهُ مَعَ الْمُزَيِّنِ قُلْنَا لِلْمُزَيِّنِ أَحَقٌّ مَا قَالَهُ هَذَا الشَّابُّ عَنْكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿnā ḥikāyatahu maʿa al-muzayyini qulnā li-al-muzayyini a-ḥaqqun mā qālahu hādhā al-shābbu ʿanka
sentences.l: And when we heard his tale with the barber, we said to the barber: Is it true, what this young man said about you?
sentences.i: When we had heard his account of his dealings with the barber, we said to the barber, "Is what this young man says of you true?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ أَنَا فَعَلْتُ مَعَهُ ذَلِكَ بِمَعْرِفَتِي وَعَقْلِي وَمُرُوَّتِي وَلَوْلَا أَنَا لَهَلَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla wa-Allāhi anā faʿaltu maʿahu dhālika bi-maʿrifatī wa-ʿaqlī wa-murūwatī wa-law-lā anā la-halaka
sentences.l: And he said: By God, I did with him that, by my knowledge and my intellect and my manliness; and had it not been for me, he would have perished.
sentences.i: He said, "By God, I did that for him out of my knowledge, my good sense and my sense of honour; and had it not been for me, he would have perished."
sentences.n: مُرُوَّة (muruwwa) is manliness, chivalry, the code of honour of a decent man; the print writes it without the second vowel letter, مروتي, and it is pointed as the common variant مُرُوَّة. It is the barber's favourite word for himself, and the ironies of this night begin with it. The barber is about to tell the caliph story that shows how "silent" he is.

sentences.t: وَمَا سَبَبُ نَجَاتِهِ إِلَّا أَنَا وَصَارَ مَلِيحًا الَّذِى أَصَابَ فِي رِجْلِهِ وَلَا أَصَابَ فِى رُوحِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-mā sababu najātihi illā anā wa-ṣāra malīḥan al-ladhī aṣāba fī rijlihi wa-lā aṣāba fī rūḥihi
sentences.l: And what (is) the cause of his rescue except me; and it became fine, that-which struck in his leg, and (nothing) struck in his spirit.
sentences.i: The only cause of his rescue was I. What befell his leg turned out well enough, and his life was not touched at all.
sentences.n: A loose sentence, pointed as printed. وَصَارَ مَلِيحًا الَّذِي أَصَابَ فِي رِجْلِهِ: "what struck his leg became fine", the barber's way of calling a broken leg a small thing; the second أَصَابَ has no stated subject ("nothing struck his life"). رُوح here is the life or person, not the soul.

sentences.t: وَلَوْ كُنْتُ كَثِيزَ الْكَلَامِ مَا فَعَلْتُ مَعَهُ الْجَمِيلَ
sentences.tr: wa-law kuntu kathīza al-kalāmi mā faʿaltu maʿahu al-jamīla
sentences.l: And if I were much-of the talk, I would not have done with him the good (deed).
sentences.i: Had I been a man of many words, I should never have done him that kindness.
sentences.n: كَثِيزَ is a misprint (zāy for rā') for كَثِيرَ, "much"; it is pointed as the letters stand and read as kathīr. الْجَمِيل, "the beautiful", is "the kind act".

sentences.t: وَهَا أَنَا أَقُولُ لَكُمْ حَدِيثًا جَرَى لِى حَتَّى تُصَدِّقُوا أَنِّي قَلِيلُ الْكَلَامِ وَمَا عِنْدِي فُضُولٌ مِنْ دُونِ إِخْوَتِي السِّتَّةِ
sentences.tr: wa-hā anā aqūlu lakum ḥadīthan jarā lī ḥattā tuṣaddiqū annī qalīlu al-kalāmi wa-mā ʿindī fuḍūlun min dūni ikhwatī al-sittati
sentences.l: And here I (am), I tell you a tale that happened to me, so that you believe that I (am) little of talk, and there is not with me meddling, apart from my six brothers.
sentences.i: Now let me tell you something that happened to me, so that you will believe I am a man of few words and no meddler, unlike my six brothers.
sentences.n: فُضُول, "surplus", is used of a person for "meddlesomeness, impertinence"; the plural form serves as a singular, as in the spoken language. مِنْ دُونِ here marks a contrast: "as distinct from my six brothers", who are as talkative as he is.

sentences.t: وَذَلِكَ أَنِّي كُنْتُ بِبَغْدَادَ عَلَى زَمَنِ الْمُسْتَنْصِرِ بِاللَّهِ ابْنِ الْمُسْتَضِى بِاللَّهِ وَكَانَ هُوَ الْخَلِيفَةَ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِبَغْدَادَ
sentences.tr: wa-dhālika annī kuntu bi-Baghdāda ʿalā zamani al-Mustanṣiri bi-Allāhi ibni al-Mustaḍī bi-Allāhi wa-kāna huwa al-khalīfata yawmaʾidhin bi-Baghdāda
sentences.l: And that (is) that I was in Baghdad in the time of al-Mustanṣir bi-Allāh, son of al-Mustaḍī bi-Allāh, and he was the caliph on that day in Baghdad.
sentences.i: It happened that I was in Baghdad in the days of al-Mustanṣir bi-Allāh, son of al-Mustaḍī bi-Allāh, who was caliph there at that time.
sentences.n: The caliph al-Mustanṣir (reigned 1226–1242) was the great-grandson, not the son, of al-Mustaḍīʾ (1170–1180); the print spells that name المستضى, without the final hamza. A thirteenth-century caliph at Baghdad is a late date for a tale that otherwise belongs with Hārūn al-Rashīd's court. بِاللَّهِ is part of each caliph's throne-name ("he who seeks victory through God").

sentences.t: وَكَانَ يُحِبُّ الْفُقَرَاءَ وَالْمَسَاكِينَ وَيُجَالِسُ الْعُلَمَاءَ وَالصَّالِحِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna yuḥibbu al-fuqarāʾa wa-al-masākīna wa-yujālisu al-ʿulamāʾa wa-al-ṣāliḥīna
sentences.l: And he used to love the poor and the destitute, and to sit-with the learned and the righteous.
sentences.i: He loved the poor and the needy, and kept company with scholars and pious men.

sentences.t: فَاتَّفَقَ لَهُ يَوْمًا أَنَّهُ غَضِبَ عَلَى عَشْرِ نَفَرٍ فَأَمَرَ الْمُتَوَلِّيَ بِبَغْدَادَ أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُ بِهِمْ يَوْمَ عِيدٍ
sentences.tr: fa-ittafaqa lahu yawman annahu ghaḍiba ʿalā ʿashri nafarin fa-amara al-mutawallī bi-Baghdāda an yaʾtiyahu bihim yawma ʿīdin
sentences.l: And it chanced for him one day that he was angry at ten persons, and he commanded the governor in Baghdad that he bring-him them, on a feast day.
sentences.i: One day it happened that he grew angry with ten men, and he ordered the prefect of Baghdad to bring them before him on a feast day.
sentences.n: الْمُتَوَلِّي, "the one put in charge", is the prefect, the officer who commands the city's police. عَشْرِ نَفَرٍ: Classical Arabic would say عَشَرَةُ نَفَرٍ, since nafar takes the feminine form of the number; the print has the bare عَشْر, pointed as printed. اتَّفَقَ لَهُ, "it fell out for him", is a stock way to begin a story.

sentences.t: وَكَانُوا لُصُوصًا قَطَّاعِينَ لِلطَّرِيقِ
sentences.tr: wa-kānū luṣūṣan qaṭṭāʿīna li-al-ṭarīqi
sentences.l: And they were thieves, cutters for the road.
sentences.i: They were thieves and highwaymen.
sentences.n: قَطَّاعِينَ لِلطَّرِيقِ, "cutters for the road": the لِـ stands in for the genitive of the Classical قَطَّاعُو الطَّرِيقِ, "cutters-of-the-road", that is, highwaymen. This use of لِـ is common in Middle Arabic.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَ مُتَوَلِّي الْبَلَدِ فَأَخَذَهُمْ وَنَزَلَ بِهِمْ فِي زَوْرَقٍ
sentences.tr: fa-kharaja mutawallī al-baladi fa-akhadhahum wa-nazala bihim fī zawraqin
sentences.l: And the governor of the town went out and took them, and he went-down with them in a skiff.
sentences.i: So the prefect of the town went out, seized them, and put out with them in a boat.
sentences.n: زَوْرَق is a small river boat, here on the Tigris. نَزَلَ بِهِمْ فِي زَوْرَقٍ, "he went down with them in a skiff", means that he took them aboard.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرْتُهُمْ أَنَا فَقُلْتُ مَا اجْتَمَعُوا هَؤُلَاءِ إِلَّا لِوَلِيمَةٍ وَأَظُنُّهُمْ يَقْطَعُونَ نَهَارَهُمْ فِي هَذَا الزَّوْرَقِ فِي أَكْلٍ وَشُرْبٍ وَمَا يَكُونُ نَدِيمَهُمْ غَيْرِي
sentences.tr: fa-naẓartuhum anā fa-qultu mā ijtamaʿū hāʾulāʾi illā li-walīmatin wa-aẓunnuhum yaqṭaʿūna nahārahum fī hādhā al-zawraqi fī aklin wa-shurbin wa-mā yakūnu nadīmahum ghayrī
sentences.l: And I looked-at them, I, and I said: These did not gather except for a feast; and I think them cutting their day in this skiff in eating and drinking, and none will be their boon-companion other-than me.
sentences.i: I watched them and said to myself, "These men have gathered only for a banquet. I expect they will pass the day in this boat eating and drinking, and they will have no companion at their cups but me."
sentences.n: نَدِيم is the "boon-companion", the friend who sits with one over wine. يَقْطَعُونَ نَهَارَهُمْ, "they cut their day", means "they pass the day". Here the barber has taken a boatload of manacled highwaymen for a party.

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ يَا جَمَاعَةُ مِنْ جُمْلَةِ مُرُوَّتِي وَرَزَانَةِ عَقْلِي نَزَلْتُ مَعَهُمْ فِي الزَّوْرَقِ وَاخْتَلَطْتُ بِهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu yā jamāʿatu min jumlati murūwatī wa-razānati ʿaqlī nazaltu maʿahum fī al-zawraqi wa-ikhtalaṭtu bihim
sentences.l: And I rose, O company, from the sum of my manliness and the steadiness of my mind: I went-down with them in the skiff, and I mingled with them.
sentences.i: So I got up, friends, out of the goodness of my nature and the steadiness of my mind, went down into the boat with them, and mixed in among them.
sentences.n: يَا جَمَاعَةُ, "O company", is the barber turning to his hearers at the feast. مِنْ جُمْلَةِ, "out of the sum of", is "as part of". نَزَلْتُ follows قُمْتُ with no conjunction. اِخْتَلَطَ بِـ is "to mingle with".

sentences.t: فَعَبَرُوا وَقَعَدُوا إِلَى الْجَانِبِ الْآخَرِ فَجَاءَتْ لَهُ شُرْطِيَّةٌ وَأَعْوَانٌ بِالْجَنَازِيرِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿabarū wa-qaʿadū ilā al-jānibi al-ākhari fa-jāʾat lahu shurṭiyyatun wa-aʿwānun bi-al-janāzīri
sentences.l: And they crossed, and they sat down at the other bank, and there came to him a police-force and helpers with the chains.
sentences.i: They crossed over and sat down on the opposite bank, and there came a squad of police and officers with chains.
sentences.n: شُرْطِيَّة is a body of police (from shurṭa, "the police"). لَهُ, "to him", is unclear: either the prefect or a slip for لَهُمْ; the pointing follows the print. الْجَنَازِير is the plural of جِنْزِير, a chain (Persian zanjīr).

sentences.t: وَرَمَوْهُمْ فِي رِقَا بِهِمْ وَرَمَوْا فِي رَقَبَتِي جِنْزِيرًا مِنْ جُمْلَتِهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-ramawhum fī riqā bihim wa-ramaw fī raqabatī jinzīran min jumlatihim
sentences.l: And they cast them in their necks, and they cast in my neck a chain from the sum of them.
sentences.i: and they flung chains about the necks of the prisoners, and one more about my neck, as though I were one of the number.
sentences.n: رِقَا بِهِمْ is one word, رِقَابِهِمْ, "their necks", split by a stray space after the alif; the second half بِهِمْ is the final bāʾ of the plural with the suffix, not a preposition. رَمَوْهُمْ, "they cast them", should have the chains as object (Classical رَمَوْهَا); the sense is plain. مِنْ جُمْلَتِهِمْ, "from the sum of them": as one of their number.

sentences.t: فَهَذَا يَا جَمَاعَةُ مَا هُوَ مِنْ مُرُوَّتِى وَقِلَّةِ كَلَامِى الَّذِي سَكَتُّ
sentences.tr: fa-hādhā yā jamāʿatu mā huwa min murūwatī wa-qillati kalāmī al-ladhī sakattu
sentences.l: So this, O company, is it not from my manliness and the fewness of my talk, that I was silent?
sentences.i: Now was this not, my friends, a mark of my honour and my fewness of words, that I kept silent?
sentences.n: The sentence is a question with no interrogative word: مَا هُوَ means "is it not". The print has only a damma on the tā' of سكتُ; the shadda is supplied to give سَكَتُّ, "I was silent", and الَّذِي here means "that".

sentences.t: وَمَا رَضِيتُ أَتَكَلَّمُ فَأَخَذُونَا بِالْجَنَازِيرِ وَقَدَّمُونَا بَيْنَ يَدَيِ الْمُسْتَنْصِرِ بِاللَّهِ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-mā raḍītu atakallamu fa-akhadhūnā bi-al-janāzīri wa-qaddamūnā bayna yadayi al-Mustanṣiri bi-Allāhi amīri al-muʾminīna
sentences.l: And I did not consent (that) I speak; and they took us with the chains, and they brought-us-forward between the two hands of al-Mustanṣir bi-Allāh, commander of the believers.
sentences.i: I did not consent to speak, and they led us off in chains and brought us before al-Mustanṣir bi-Allāh, Commander of the Faithful.
sentences.n: رَضِيتُ أَتَكَلَّمُ: "I was content (to) speak", again with no linking أَنْ. بَيْنَ يَدَيِ, "between the two hands of", means "in the presence of".

sentences.t: فَأَمَرَ بِضَرْبِ رِقَابِ الْعَشَرَةِ فَتَقَدَّمَ السَّيَّافُ بَعْدَ أَنْ أَجْلَسَنَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ فِي نِطْعِ الدَّمِ
sentences.tr: fa-amara bi-ḍarbi riqābi al-ʿasharati fa-taqaddama al-sayyāfu baʿda an ajlasanā bayna yadayhi fī niṭʿi al-dami
sentences.l: And he commanded the striking of the necks of the ten, and the swordsman came-forward after (one) had seated us between his two hands on the leather-of-blood.
sentences.i: He ordered the ten beheaded, and the executioner stepped forward, after we had been seated before him on the blood mat.
sentences.n: نِطْع is the leather mat spread under a condemned man so that the blood does not stain the floor; نِطْعُ الدَّمِ is "the blood mat". أَجْلَسَنَا is pointed as active, "he (that is, the guards) made us sit", but "we were seated" would do as well. السَّيَّاف, "the man of the sword", is the executioner.

sentences.t: وَجَرَّدَ سَيْفَهُ وَضَرَبَ رَقَبَةَ وَاحِدٍ بَعْدَ وَاحِدٍ إِلَى أَنْ ضَرَبَ رَقَبَةَ الْعَشَرَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-jarrada sayfahu wa-ḍaraba raqabata wāḥidin baʿda wāḥidin ilā an ḍaraba raqabata al-ʿasharati
sentences.l: And he drew his sword, and he struck the neck of one after one, until he had struck the neck of the ten;
sentences.i: He drew his sword and struck off the heads one after another, until he had dealt with the ten,
sentences.n: The print has the singular رَقَبَة, "the neck", here against the plural رِقَاب in the lines before and after; it is pointed as printed. The executioner thinks he has done all ten, which is the barber's joke on him.

sentences.t: فَبَقِيتُ أَنَا فَنَظَرَ الْخَلِيفَةُ فَقَالَ لِلسَّيَّافِ مَا بَالُكَ ضَرَبْتَ رِقَابَ تِسْعَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-baqītu anā fa-naẓara al-khalīfatu fa-qāla li-al-sayyāfi mā bāluka ḍarabta riqāba tisʿatin
sentences.l: And I remained, I; and the caliph looked, and he said to the swordsman: What (is) your state, (that) you struck the necks of nine?
sentences.i: but I was left over. The Caliph looked and said to the executioner, "What is the matter with you? You have struck off the heads of nine!"
sentences.n: مَا بَالُكَ is a stock phrase, "what is your condition?", i.e. "what is wrong with you?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَ السَّيَّافُ مَعَاذَاللَّهِ أَنْ تَأْمُرَ بِضَرْبِ رِقَابِ عَشَرَةٍ فَأَضْرِبَ أَنَا رِقَابَ تِسْعَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-sayyāfu maʿādha Allāhi an taʾmura bi-ḍarbi riqābi ʿasharatin fa-aḍriba anā riqāba tisʿatin
sentences.l: And the swordsman said: God's-refuge, that you command the striking of the necks of ten and I then-strike, I, the necks of nine!
sentences.i: The executioner answered, "God forbid that you should order ten heads struck off and I should strike off nine!"
sentences.n: مَعَاذَ اللَّهِ, "the refuge of God", is "God forbid"; the print writes the two words as one, مَعَاذَاللَّهِ, and that is kept. The verbs after أَنْ and فَـ are subjunctive: "that you command ... and I strike".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ مَا أَظُنُّكَ ضَرَبْتَ رِقَابَ غَيْرِ تِسْعَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu mā aẓunnuka ḍarabta riqāba ghayri tisʿatin
sentences.l: And he said to him: I do not think you struck the necks of other-than nine,
sentences.i: The caliph said to him, "I think you have struck off the heads of nine and no more,
sentences.n: The speaker is the caliph. The sentence runs on into the next unit; the print has a stray و at the end of this line (see the next note).

sentences.t: وَ هَذَا الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ هُوَالْعَاشِرُ
sentences.tr: wa-hādhā al-ladhī bayna yadayka huwa al-ʿāshiru
sentences.l: and this one who (is) between your two hands, he (is) the tenth.
sentences.i: and this man who sits before you is the tenth."
sentences.n: The print leaves a space after the wāw (وَ هَذَا) and runs هُوَ and الْعَاشِرُ together (هُوَالْعَاشِرُ); both are kept as printed, and the text is pointed as it stands. The caliph points at the barber.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ السَّيَّافُ وَحَقِّ نِعْمَتِكَ إِنَّهُمْ عَشَرَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-sayyāfu wa-ḥaqqi niʿmatika innahum ʿasharatun
sentences.l: And the swordsman said: By the right of your favour, they are ten.
sentences.i: The executioner said, "By your bounty, there are ten of them!"
sentences.n: وَحَقِّ نِعْمَتِكَ, "by the right of your favour", is an oath a servant swears by his master's kindness to him.

sentences.t: قَالَ فَعَلَ وَهُمْ فَإِذَا هُمْ عَشَرَةٌ
sentences.tr: qāla faʿala wa-hum fa-idhā hum ʿasharatun
sentences.l: He said: so did, and they; and behold, they (were) ten.
sentences.i: "Count them," said the Caliph; and when they were counted, there were ten.
sentences.n: The print's فعل وهم does not read as Arabic. The sense, after "and behold, they were ten", is "count them", فَعُدُّوهُمْ, with the lām a misprint for dāl and the word broken by a stray space; the translation follows that, but the pointing follows the letters (فَعَلَ, "he did", وَهُمْ, "and they"). Only nine heads had been struck, and the tenth was the barber, which is how the count came out at ten.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَ إِلَىَّ الْخَلِيفَةُ وَقَالَ مَا حَمَلَكَ عَلَى سُكُوتِكَ فِي مِثْلِ هَذَا الْوَقْتِ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓara ilayya al-khalīfatu wa-qāla mā ḥamalaka ʿalā sukūtika fī mithli hādhā al-waqti
sentences.l: And the caliph looked to-me and said: What bore you upon your silence in the like of this time?
sentences.i: The caliph looked at me and said, "What made you keep silent at such a moment,
sentences.n: The print writes الى for both إِلَى, "to", and إِلَيَّ, "to me"; here it can only be "to me", with الْخَلِيفَةُ as the subject, so the ي takes the shadda. حَمَلَ عَلَى is "to bring someone to do something".

sentences.t: وَكَيْفَ صِرْتَ مَعَ أَصْحَابِ الدَّمِ
sentences.tr: wa-kayfa ṣirta maʿa aṣḥābi al-dami
sentences.l: and how did you come to be with the possessors of blood?
sentences.i: and how did you come to be among men of blood?
sentences.n: أَصْحَابُ الدَّمِ, "the people of blood", are the condemned killers. The caliph's question carries on into the next line, with a further "and what is the reason for this".

sentences.t: وَمَا سَبَبُ هَذَا وَأَنْتَ شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ وَعَقْلُكَ قَلِيلٌ
sentences.tr: wa-mā sababu hādhā wa-anta shaykhun kabīrun wa-ʿaqluka qalīlun
sentences.l: and what (is) the cause of this, and you (are) an old shaykh, and your mind (is) little
sentences.i: and what is the reason for this, when you are a man of great age and little sense?
sentences.n: The first words are the tail of the Caliph's question to the barber (the slice begins mid-speech). وَأَنْتَ is the circumstantial wāw, "while you are…": how can a grey old man have so little judgment?

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ خِطَابَ أَمِيرِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ قُلْتُ لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu khiṭāba amīri al-muʾminīna qultu lahu
sentences.l: and when I heard the address of the commander-of-the-believers, I said to him
sentences.i: When I heard the Commander of the Faithful's words, I said to him,
sentences.n: The print joins اميرالمؤمنين into one word here and in the next sentence; it is vocalised as printed. The barber now takes up the story in his own voice.

sentences.t: اِعْلَمْ بَا أَمِيرَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِنِّي أَنَا الشَّيْخُ الصَّامِتُ وَعِنْدِي مِنَ الْحِكْمَةِ شَيٌ كَثِيرٌ
sentences.tr: iʿlam bā amīra al-muʾminīna innī anā al-shaykhu al-ṣāmitu wa-ʿindī mina al-ḥikmati shayʾun kathīrun
sentences.l: know, O commander-of-the-believers, indeed I, I (am) the shaykh the Silent, and with me (is) of wisdom a-thing many
sentences.i: Know, Commander of the Faithful, that I am the Silent Shaykh, and I have a great deal of wisdom.
sentences.n: The print has با where يا ("O") is meant, a slip of the dots; it is pointed as printed. In شيٌ the print itself marks the tanwīn and drops the hamza: read shayʾun, "a thing"; مِنَ الْحِكْمَةِ شَيْءٌ كَثِيرٌ is "a great deal of wisdom" (partitive min). إِنِّي أَنَا is emphatic, "I, I myself". الشَّيْخُ الصَّامِتُ is the barber's own boastful title, taken from his name al-Ṣāmit.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا رَزَانَةُ عَقْلِي وَجَوْدَةُ فَهْمِي وَقِلَّةُ كَلَامِي لَا نِهَايَةَ لَهَا وَصَنْعَتِي مُزَيِّنٌ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā razānatu ʿaqlī wa-jawdatu fahmī wa-qillatu kalāmī lā nihāyata lahā wa-ṣanʿatī muzayyinun
sentences.l: and as-for the steadiness of my mind and the excellence of my understanding and the fewness of my speech, no end to it; and my craft (is) barber
sentences.i: As for the steadiness of my mind, the soundness of my understanding and the fewness of my words, there is no end to them; and my trade is barbering.
sentences.n: وَأَمَّا … can be followed by an unmarked new clause: the three nouns are a hanging topic ("as for…"), picked up by -hā in لَهَا. لَا نِهَايَةَ لَهَا ("no end to it") is the tone of a man praising his own virtues; the irony that the barber is the least silent man in the Nights is the joke of the whole cycle.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ نَهَارُ أَمْسِ مِنْ بَاكِرِ النَّهَارِ نَظَرْتُ هَؤُلَاءِ الْعَشَرَةَ قَاصِدِينَ الزَّوْرَقَ فَاخْتَلَطْتُ بِهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna nahāru amsi min bākiri al-nahāri naẓartu hāʾulāʾi al-ʿasharata qāṣidīna al-zawraqa fa-ikhtalaṭtu bihim
sentences.l: and when it was the day of yesterday, from the early-part of the day, I looked (at) these ten, intending the skiff, and I mingled with them
sentences.i: Yesterday, early in the day, I saw these ten men making for the boat, and I mixed in among them,
sentences.n: نَهَارُ أَمْسِ, "yesterday's day", is simply "yesterday". نَظَرْتُ takes a direct object here ("I looked at"), and قَاصِدِينَ is a circumstantial participle, accusative, "intending, heading for". الزَّوْرَقُ is the skiff or light river-boat of the Tigris. بِهِمْ after اخْتَلَطَ marks the company one mingles with.

sentences.t: وَنَزَلْتُ مَعَهُمْ وَظَنَنْتُ أَنَّهُمْ فِي وَلِيمَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-nazaltu maʿahum wa-ẓanantu annahum fī walīmatin
sentences.l: and I went-down with them, and I thought that they (were) at a banquet
sentences.i: and went down with them, supposing that they were bound for a feast.

sentences.t: فَمَا كَانَ غَيْرَ سَاعَةٍ إِلَّا حَضَرَتْ إِلَيْهِمُ الْأَعْوَانُ وَجَعَلُوا فِي رِقَابِهِمُ الْجَنَازِيرَ وَجَعَلُوا فِي رَقَبَتِي جَنْزِيرًا مِنْ جُمْلَتِهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-mā kāna ghayra sāʿatin illā ḥaḍarat ilayhimu al-aʿwānu wa-jaʿalū fī riqābihimu al-janāzīra wa-jaʿalū fī raqabatī janzīran min jumlatihim
sentences.l: and it was not other-than an hour but there-attended to-them the helpers, and they put in their necks the chains, and they put in my neck a chain from the whole-of-them
sentences.i: Within the hour the officers were upon them; they put chains on the necks of the ten, and they put a chain on my neck too, as one of the company.
sentences.n: فَمَا كَانَ غَيْرَ سَاعَةٍ إِلَّا … is the idiom "it was no more than an hour before…". The verb حَضَرَتْ is feminine singular before a plural subject that follows it, which is correct for a broken plural (الْأَعْوَانُ, "the helpers", i.e. the Caliph's officers or guards). مِنْ جُمْلَتِهِمْ, "from the sum of them", means "as one of them, reckoned among them".

sentences.t: فَمِنْ كَثْرَةِ مُرُوَّتِي سَكَتَّ وَلَمْ أَتَكَلَّمْ فَمَا هِيَ إِلَّامُرُوَّةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-min kathrati murūwatī sakatta wa-lam atakallam fa-mā hiya illāmurūwatun
sentences.l: and from the abundance of my manliness I was silent and did not speak, and it was nothing but manliness
sentences.i: Out of sheer chivalry I kept silent and did not speak, for it was nothing but chivalry.
sentences.n: مُرُوَّة (murūwa, in the print without the hamza of مروءة) is the manly virtue of generosity, loyalty and decorum: here the barber's account of why he said nothing. The print marks سكتَّ with a fatha and shadda, which would be sakatta ("you were silent"); the sense requires sakattu ("I was silent"), so the printed mark is kept and the slip flagged. إلا مروة is printed as one word, الامروة; it is pointed as printed.

sentences.t: فَسَارُوا بِنَا حَتَّى أَوْقَفُونَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ فَأَمَرْتَ بِضَرْبِ رِقَابِ الْعَشَرَةِ وَبَقِيتُ أَنَا بَيْنَ يَدَيِ السَّيَّافِ وَلَمْ أُعَرِّفْكُمْ بِنَفْسِي
sentences.tr: fa-sārū binā ḥattā awqafūnā bayna yadayka fa-amarta bi-ḍarbi riqābi al-ʿasharati wa-baqītu anā bayna yaday al-sayyāfi wa-lam uʿarrifkum bi-nafsī
sentences.l: and they went with us until they made-us-stand between your two hands, and you commanded the striking of the necks of the ten, and I remained, I, between the two hands of the sword-bearer, and I did not make-known to-you with myself
sentences.i: They marched us off until they stood us before you, and you ordered the ten beheaded. I was left standing before the executioner, and I did not make myself known to you.
sentences.n: بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ, "between your two hands", is the standard way to say "in your presence". أَمَرَ بِـ takes the thing commanded with بِـ: "he commanded the striking-of-necks". السَّيَّاف is the sword-man, the executioner. لَمْ أُعَرِّفْكُمْ بِنَفْسِي: the verb is of the form I ("to make known"), taken in the print as unmarked أعرفكم; the second-person plural -kum addresses the Caliph with the respectful plural.

sentences.t: فَمَا هِيَ إِلَّا مُرُوَّةٌ عَظِيمَةٌ الَّتِى شَارَكْتُهُمْ فِيهَا فِى الْقَتْلِ
sentences.tr: fa-mā hiya illā murūwatun ʿaẓīmatun allatī shārakutuhum fīhā fī al-qatli
sentences.l: and it is nothing but a great manliness, that which I shared them in it in the killing
sentences.i: It was nothing but a great act of chivalry, by which I shared the killing with them.
sentences.n: الَّتِى is printed with final ى; it is the feminine relative picking up مُرُوَّة, and فِيهَا is the resumptive pronoun ("in which"). The sentence is hardly plain Classical: strictly it should read "the chivalry in which I shared with them in being killed".

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ طُولَ دَهْرِي هَكَذَا أَفْعَلُ الْجَمِيلَ مَعَ النَّاسِ وَهُمْ يُكَافِئُونَنِي بِأَوْحَشِ مُكَافَاتٍ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin ṭūla dahrī hākadhā afʿalu al-jamīla maʿa al-nāsi wa-hum yukāfiʾūnanī bi-awḥashi mukāfātin
sentences.l: but the length of my time thus I do the beautiful with the people, and they repay-me with the most-desolate of repayments
sentences.i: But all my life I have done what is fair by people, and they repay me with the vilest of returns.
sentences.n: طُولَ دَهْرِي, "the length of my age", is an adverbial accusative, "all my life". أَوْحَشِ is a superlative ("most desolate, most savage") in an iḍāfa with a plural. The print gives مكافات where the plural مكافآت is expected; it is pointed as the sound feminine plural of مُكَافَاة, repayment.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْخَلِيفَةُ كَلَامِي وَعَلِمَ أَنِّي كَثِيرُ الْمُرُوَّةِ قَلِيلُ الْكَلَامِ مَا عِنْدِي فُضُولٌ كَمَا يَزْعُمُ هَذَا الشَّابُّ الَّذِي خَلَّصْتُهُ مِنَ الْأَهْوَالِ ضَحِكَ ضَحِكًا شَدِيدًا حَتَّى اسْتَلْقَى عَلَى قَفَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-khalīfatu kalāmī wa-ʿalima annī kathīru al-murūwati qalīlu al-kalāmi mā ʿindī fuḍūlun ka-mā yazʿumu hādhā al-shābbu al-ladhī khallaṣtuhu mina al-ahwāli ḍaḥika ḍaḥikan shadīdan ḥattā istalqā ʿalā qafāhu
sentences.l: and when the caliph heard my speech and knew that I (am) many-of manliness, few-of speech, there is not with me meddling as this young-man claims, the one-who I rescued him from the terrors, he laughed a strong laughing until he fell-on-his-back upon his nape
sentences.i: When the Caliph heard my words, and learned that I was a man of great chivalry and few words, with none of the meddling this young man claims, this man whom I had rescued from his terrors, he laughed so hard that he fell over backwards.
sentences.n: كَمَا here is "as, in the way that", and مَا عِنْدِي فُضُولٌ ("there is not with me meddling") is the barber's self-defence against the young man's charge that he is an officious busybody. الَّذِي خَلَّصْتُهُ is a relative with a resumptive -hu. اسْتَلْقَى عَلَى قَفَاهُ is "to throw oneself on one's back", from the nape. The barber of course claims here that he rescued the lame youth; the young man's version, told earlier in the Night cycle, is rather different.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَايِفَةُ لِي يَاصَامِتُ وَ إِخْوَتُكَ السِّتَّةُ مِثْلُكَ فِيهِمُ الْحِكْمَةُ وَ الْعِلْمُ وَ قِلَّةُ الْكَلَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khāyifatu lī yā ṣāmitu wa-ikhwatuka al-sittatu mithluka fīhimu al-ḥikmatu wa-al-ʿilmu wa-qillatu al-kalāmi
sentences.l: and the caliph said to me: O Silent, and your brothers the six (are) like you, in them (is) the wisdom and the knowledge and the fewness of the speech
sentences.i: And the Caliph said to me, "Silent One, are your six brothers like you, with wisdom and learning and few words?"
sentences.n: The print spells the caliph الخايفة, with yā' for lām; this is read as printed (khāyifa) and is a slip for الخليفة. يَاصَامِتُ is printed as one word, a vocative with the name in the nominative. The detached و ("و اخوتك", "و العلم", "و قلة") is the edition's spacing, kept as printed. The sentence is a question without an interrogative particle, carried by intonation.

sentences.t: قُلْتُ لَاعَاشُوا وَ لَابَقُوا إِنْ كَانُوا مِثْلِي
sentences.tr: qultu lā ʿāshū wa-lā baqū in kānū mithlī
sentences.l: I said: may-they-not live, and may-they-not remain, if they are like me
sentences.i: I said, "May they not live, may they not last, if they are like me!"
sentences.n: لَا عَاشُوا وَلَا بَقُوا is the curse-formula "may they not live, may they not stay", the perfect with لا in the sense of a wish. The two verbs are printed joined to لا (لاعاشوا, لابقوا), kept as printed.

sentences.t: وَ لَكِنْ ذَمَّيْتَنِي يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin dhammaytanī yā amīra al-muʾminīna
sentences.l: but you have blamed-me, O commander-of-the-believers
sentences.i: But you have disparaged me, Commander of the Faithful,
sentences.n: ذَمَّيْتَنِي is Middle Arabic: the geminate ذَمَّ ("to blame") is conjugated like a weak verb (ذَمَّيْتَ for classical ذَمَمْتَ), as with حَسِيتُ earlier in the cycle. The printed shadda is on the mīm.

sentences.t: وَلَايَنْبَغِي لَكَ أَنْ تُقَارِنَ إِخْوَتِي بِى
sentences.tr: wa-lā yanbaghī laka an tuqārina ikhwatī bī
sentences.l: and it is not fitting for you that you compare my brothers with me
sentences.i: and it is not fitting for you to set my brothers beside me,
sentences.n: لَا يَنْبَغِي لَكَ أَنْ …, "it is not fitting for you to…", takes the subjunctive; بِى is printed with final ى. قَارَنَ بِـ means "to join, compare something with something".

sentences.t: لِأَنَّهُمْ مِنْ كَثْرَةِ كَلَامِهِمْ وَ قِلَّةِ مُرُوَّتِهِمْ صَارَ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمْ بِعَاهَةٍ
sentences.tr: li-annahum min kathrati kalāmihim wa-qillati murūwatihim ṣāra kullu wāḥidin minhum bi-ʿāhatin
sentences.l: because-they, from the abundance of their speech and the fewness of their manliness, there-became each one of them with a blemish
sentences.i: for it is by reason of their much talk and little chivalry that every one of them has come to a blemish:
sentences.n: لِأَنَّهُمْ gives the reason; the clause after it has no خَبَر in the usual place, so the sentence is anacoluthic, which suits Middle Arabic. صَارَ بِعَاهَةٍ, "became with a defect", is "was afflicted with a disability"; عَاهَة (ʿāha) is a blight or bodily defect, and the enumeration that follows is the barber's list of his brothers' infirmities.

sentences.t: فَمِنْهُمْ وَاحِدٌ أَعْوَرُ وَوَاحِدًا فُلِجَ وَ وَاحِدٌ مَقْطُوعُ الْأُذُنِ وَ الْمَنْخِرِ وَ وَاحِدٌ مَقْطُوعُ الشَّفَتَيْنِ وَ وَاحِدٌ أَحْدَبُ
sentences.tr: fa-minhum wāḥidun aʿwaru wa-wāḥidan fulija wa-wāḥidun maqṭūʿu al-udhuni wa-al-minkhari wa-wāḥidun maqṭūʿu al-shafatayni wa-wāḥidun aḥdabu
sentences.l: and of them one one-eyed, and one he-was-paralysed, and one cut-of the ear and the nostril, and one cut-of the two lips, and one hunchbacked
sentences.i: One of them is blind in one eye; one is paralysed; one has lost an ear and a nostril; one has lost both lips; and one is a hunchback.
sentences.n: A list in the nominative, but the second item is printed وواحدا with an accusative ending, as if governed by a lost verb; it is pointed as printed. فلج: the print gives only the three consonants, and I read it as the passive فُلِجَ ("was struck with palsy"); فَالِج ("palsied") is the other possibility. مَقْطُوعُ الْأُذُنِ is "cut-of-the-ear", i.e. with the ear cut off. منخر (nose or nostril) is joined to الاذن by "and" within one cut. أَعْوَرُ is one-eyed, and أَحْدَبُ is hunchbacked, the figure of the first brother, whose tale comes next.

sentences.t: وَ لَاتَحْسَبْ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنِّي كَثِيرُ الْكَلَامِ وَلَا بُدَّأَنْ أُبَيِّنَ لَكَ وَ أَنِّي أَعْظَمُ مُرُوَّةً مِنْهُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-lā taḥsab yā amīra al-muʾminīna annī kathīru al-kalāmi wa-lā budda an ubayyina laka wa-annī aʿẓamu muruwwatan minhum
sentences.l: And do not reckon, O commander of-the-believers, that I am much of-speech; and there is no escape that I make-plain to-you, and that I am greater in manliness than-them.
sentences.i: And do not think, Commander of the Faithful, that I am a man of many words. I must make it plain to you that I am greater in chivalry than they.
sentences.n: The print runs لا بد and أن together as بدان and leaves a stray space after the first و; both are kept as printed. The phrase is lā budda an, "there is no escaping that", so "I must". مروة is printed without the hamza of classical مُرُوءَة and is pointed muruwwa: manliness, honourable conduct. The barber is about to set his own decency against his brothers' defects (and so, ironically, to talk at length).

sentences.t: وَلِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمْ حِكَايَةٌ اِتَّفَقَتْ لَهُ حَتَّى صَارَفِيهِ عَاهَةٌ وَأَنَا أَحْكِى لَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-li-kulli wāḥidin minhum ḥikāyatun ittafaqat lahu ḥattā ṣāra fīhi ʿāhatun wa-anā aḥkī laka
sentences.l: And to-each one of-them (is) a story that befell to-him, until there-became in-him a defect; and I relate to-you.
sentences.i: Each of them has a story of what befell him, until he was left with a defect, and I will tell them to you.
sentences.n: صارفيه is two words run together in the print, ṣāra fīhi, "there came to be in him". ʿāha is a blemish or infirmity, here the bodily defects listed a moment ago. أحكي is the first-person imperfect "I relate", with the weak final letter written ى.

sentences.t: اِعْلَمْ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنَّ الْأَوَّلَ وَ هُوَ الْأَحْدَبُ كَانَ صَنْعَتُهُ الْخِيَاطَةَ بِبَغْدَادَ
sentences.tr: iʿlam yā amīra al-muʾminīna anna al-awwala wa-huwa al-aḥdabu kāna ṣanʿatuhu al-khiyāṭata bi-Baghdāda
sentences.l: Know, O commander of-the-believers, that the first, and he (is) the hunchback, his-trade was the sewing, in Baghdad.
sentences.i: Know, Commander of the Faithful, that the first, the hunchback, was a tailor by trade in Baghdad.
sentences.n: كان صنعته الخياطة is "his trade was tailoring": the thing described (ṣanʿatuhu) is the subject of kāna and the trade named (al-khiyāṭata) its predicate, hence the accusative. Baghdād is a diptote, so after bi- it takes the fatḥa.

sentences.t: فَكَانَ يَخِيطُ فِي دُكَّانٍ اِسْتَأْجَرَهَا مِنْ رَجُلٍ كَثِيرِ الْمَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-kāna yakhīṭu fī dukkānin istaʾjarahā min rajulin kathīri al-māli
sentences.l: And he was sewing in a shop that-he-rented-it from a man much of-the-wealth.
sentences.i: He used to sew in a shop that he rented from a very rich man.
sentences.n: The relative clause has no relative pronoun and repeats its noun as a pronoun (dukkān ... istaʾjarahā, "a shop he rented it"), which is ordinary in Middle Arabic; dukkān is treated as feminine here.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ الرَّجُلُ سَاكِنًا عَلَى الدُّكَّانِ وَ كَانَ فِي أَسْفَلِ دَارِ الرَّجُلِ طَاحُونًا
sentences.tr: wa-kāna dhālika al-rajulu sākinan ʿalā al-dukkāni wa-kāna fī asfali dāri al-rajuli ṭāḥūnan
sentences.l: And that man was dwelling above the shop; and there was in the lower-part of the house of-the-man a mill.
sentences.i: The man lived above the shop, and on the ground floor of his house there was a mill.
sentences.n: طاحونا is accusative although it is the thing that "was" (the subject of kāna), where classical Arabic would have ṭāḥūnun; the print has the ending, so it is pointed as printed. A mill below the house matters later in the tale.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا أَخِي الْأَحْدَبُ جَالِسٌ فِى الدُّكَّانِ فِي بَعْضِ الْأَ يَّامِ يَخِيطُ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā akhī al-aḥdabu jālisun fī al-dukkāni fī baʿḍi al-ayyāmi yakhīṭu
sentences.l: And while my brother the hunchback (was) sitting in the shop, on some of-the-days, sewing,
sentences.i: One day, as my brother the hunchback sat sewing in the shop,
sentences.n: الا يام is printed with a space after the alif (al-ayyām, "the days"); the two pieces are kept apart. The clause is left hanging until the next unit gives the main verb.

sentences.t: فَرَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ فَرَأَى اِمْرَأَةً كَالْبَدْرِ الطَّالِعِ فِي رَوْشَنِ الدَّارِ وَ هِيَ تَنْظُرُ إِلَى النَّاسِ
sentences.tr: fa-rafaʿa raʾsahu fa-raʾā imraʾatan ka-al-badri al-ṭāliʿi fī rawshani al-dāri wa-hiya tanẓuru ilā al-nāsi
sentences.l: And he raised his head and saw a woman like the full-moon the-rising, in the bay-window of-the-house, and she (was) looking at the people.
sentences.i: He raised his head and saw a woman like the rising full moon, at the bay window of the house, looking out at the people.
sentences.n: The full moon (badr) is the stock image of a beautiful face. روشن rawshan (from Persian) is a projecting window or balcony, usually latticed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهَا أَخِي تَعَلَّقَ قَلْبُهُ بِحُبِّهَا وَ صَارَ يَوْمَهُ ذَلِكَ يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهَا فَبَطَّلَ أَخِي خِيَاطَتَهُ إِلَى وَقْتِ الْمَسَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhā akhī taʿallaqa qalbuhu bi-ḥubbihā wa-ṣāra yawmahu dhālika yanẓuru ilayhā fa-baṭṭala akhī khiyāṭatahu ilā waqti al-masāʾi
sentences.l: And when my brother saw her, his heart clung to her love, and he became, that day of-his, looking at her; and my brother left-idle his sewing until the time of-the-evening.
sentences.i: When my brother saw her, his heart was caught in love of her, and he spent that whole day gazing at her; he abandoned his sewing until evening.
sentences.n: تعلق قلبه بـ is "his heart hung upon", the usual way of saying someone fell in love. يومه ذلك is an accusative of time ("that day of his"). I read فبطل as baṭṭala (form II, "to put out of work, leave idle"), which takes خياطته as its object.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ الْيَوْمُ الثَّانِي وَقْتَ الصَّبَاحِ فَتَحَ دُكَّانَهُ وَ قَعَدَ يَخِيطُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna al-yawmu al-thānī waqta al-ṣabāḥi fataḥa dukkānahu wa-qaʿada yakhīṭu
sentences.l: And when it was the day the-second, at-the-time of-the-morning, he opened his shop and sat sewing,
sentences.i: When the second day came, at morning, he opened his shop and sat down to sew,

sentences.t: وَ هُوَ كُلَّمَا غَرَزَ غَرْزَةً يَنْظُرُ إِلَى الرَّوْشَنِ فَرَآهَا عَلَى تِلْكَ الْحَالَةِ فَازْدَادَ حُبُّهُ لَهَا وَ هَيَامُهُ فِيهَا
sentences.tr: wa-huwa kullamā gharaza gharzatan yanẓuru ilā al-rawshani fa-raʾāhā ʿalā tilka al-ḥālati fa-izdāda ḥubbuhu lahā wa-hayāmuhu fīhā
sentences.l: and he, every-time he-pricked a stitch, looks to the bay-window; and he saw her in that state, and his love for-her increased, and his frenzy in-her.
sentences.i: and every time he drew a stitch he looked up at the window. He saw her there as before, and his love for her grew, and his frenzy over her.
sentences.n: هيام hiyām is love bordering on madness, a parched, distracted longing. فازداد is form VIII of زاد ("to increase"), with the infix letter ت turned into د after ز.

sentences.t: وَ لَمَّا كَانَ الْيَوْمُ الثَّالِثُ جَلَسَ فِي مَكَانِهِ وَهُوَ يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-lammā kāna al-yawmu al-thālithu jalasa fī makānihi wa-huwa yanẓuru ilayhā
sentences.l: And when it was the day the-third, he sat in his place, and he looking at her.
sentences.i: When the third day came, he sat in his place, gazing at her.

sentences.t: فَرَأَنْهُ الْامْرَأَةُ وَعَلِمَتْ أَنَّهُ قَدْ صَارَ أَسِيرًا لِحُبِّهَا فَضَحِكَتْ فِي وَجْهِهِ وَضَحِكَ فِي وَجْهِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-raʾanhu al-imraʾatu wa-ʿalimat annahu qad ṣāra asīran li-ḥubbihā fa-ḍaḥikat fī wajhihi wa-ḍaḥika fī wajhihā
sentences.l: And the woman saw him, and she knew that he had become a captive to her love; and she laughed in his face, and he laughed in her face.
sentences.i: The woman saw him and knew that he had become a captive of his love for her, and she laughed in his face, and he laughed in hers.
sentences.n: فرانه as printed has ن where the sense wants ت: it should be فرأته, fa-raʾat-hu, "and she saw him". I point the letters the print has and leave the slip visible. The article is attached to the whole word in الامرأة, al-imraʾa (classical al-marʾa). لحبها: li- here marks what he is a captive to, "captive to love of her".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا غَابَتْ عَلَيْهِ وَأَرْسَلَتْ جَارِيَتَهَا إِلَيْهِ وَمَعَهَا بُقْشَةٌ فِيهَا طَاقَةُ مُشَجَّرٍ أَحْمَرَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā ghābat ʿalayhi wa-arsalat jāriyatahā ilayhi wa-maʿahā buqshatun fīhā ṭāqatu mushajjarin aḥmara
sentences.l: Then indeed-she withdrew from-him, and sent her girl to him, and with her a bundle, in-it a length of figured red.
sentences.i: Then she withdrew from his sight and sent her maid to him, bringing a bundle in which was a length of red patterned cloth.
sentences.n: بقشة buqsha is a cloth bundle, from Turkish. طاقة ṭāqa is a length or bolt of cloth. مشجر mushajjar is "patterned with branches", i.e. figured. The print gives no case; I read طاقة مشجر أحمر as an iḍāfa with adjective, "a length of red figured stuff". The same reading is used below for أطلس أصفر.

sentences.t: فَجَاءَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ إِلَيْهِ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ سِتِّي تُقْرِئُكَ السَّلَامَ وَتَقُولُ لَكَ فَصِّلْ لَهَا بِيَدِ الْفَضْلِ قَمِيصًا مِنْ هَذِهِ الطَّاقَةِ وَ خَيِّطْ خِيَاطَةً حَسَنَةً
sentences.tr: fa-jāʾati al-jāriyatu ilayhi wa-qālat lahu sittī tuqriʾuka al-salāma wa-taqūlu laka faṣṣil lahā bi-yadi al-faḍli qamīṣan min hādhihi al-ṭāqati wa-khayyiṭ khiyāṭatan ḥasanatan
sentences.l: And the girl came to him and said to him: My lady makes-you-recite the greeting, and says to you: Cut-out for her, by the hand of favour, a shirt from this length, and sew a sewing good.
sentences.i: The maid came to him and said, "My lady sends you her greetings, and she says: Be so kind as to cut her a shirt from this piece, and sew it well."
sentences.n: ستي sitt, "my lady", is a shortened form of sayyidatī. تقرئك السلام (literally "makes you read the greeting") is the formula for conveying greetings. بيد الفضل ("by the hand of favour") I take as "out of your kindness". Note that the lady speaks of herself in the third person: faṣṣil lahā, "cut for her".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا سَمْعًا وَ طَاعَةً ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ فَصَّلَ لَهَا ثَوْبًا وَأَتَمَّ خِيَاطَتَهُ فِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan thumma innahu faṣṣala lahā thawban wa-atamma khiyāṭatahu fī dhālika al-yawmi
sentences.l: And he said to-her: Hearing and obedience. Then indeed-he cut-out for her a garment and completed its sewing on that day.
sentences.i: He said to her, "With hearing and obedience." Then he cut her a garment and finished sewing it that same day.
sentences.n: سمعا وطاعة is the formula of assent: the accusatives stand for "(I answer) with hearing and obedience". It recurs below.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ مِنَ الْغَدِ بَاكَرَتْهُ الْجَارِيَةُ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ سِتِّي تُسَلِّمُ عَلَيْكَ وَتَقُولُ لَكَ كَيْفَ كَانَ مَبِيتُكَ الْبَارِحَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna min al-ghadi bākarathu al-jāriyatu wa-qālat lahu sittī tusallimu ʿalayka wa-taqūlu laka kayfa kāna mabītuka al-bāriḥata
sentences.l: And when it was from the morrow, the girl came-early-to him and said to him: My lady gives-greeting upon you and says to you: How was your night-spending, last night?
sentences.i: The next morning the maid came to him early and said, "My lady greets you and asks how you passed last night.
sentences.n: كان من الغد is the idiom "when the morrow came". مبيت mabīt is the spending of the night, here a polite enquiry after how he slept (the answer, with a smile, is that he did not).

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهَا مَاذَا قَتِ النَّوْمَ مِنْ شُغْلِ قَلْبِهَا لَكَ ثُمَّ قَدَّمَتْ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ طَاقَةَ أَطْلَسٍ أَصْفَرَ
sentences.tr: fa-innahā mā dhā qati al-nawma min shughli qalbihā laka thumma qaddamat bayna yadayhi ṭāqata aṭlasin aṣfara
sentences.l: For indeed-she, not she-tasted the sleep, from the preoccupation of-her-heart with-you. Then she put-forward between his two-hands a length of satin yellow.
sentences.i: She has not tasted sleep, so taken up is her heart with you." Then she laid before him a length of yellow satin
sentences.n: ماذا قت is one word, mā dhāqat ("she did not taste"), broken in two by a space in the print; the pointing keeps the two printed pieces. أطلس aṭlas is satin. بين يديه ("between his two hands") means "before him". The maid's speech, begun in the previous unit, ends with the explanation of her mistress's sleeplessness.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لَهُ تَقُولُ لَكَ سِتِّي فَصِّلْ لَهَا مِنْ هَذِهِ الطَّاقَةِ سِرْوَالَيْنِ وَخَيِّطْهُمَا الْيَوْمَ هَذَا
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahu taqūlu laka sittī faṣṣil lahā min hādhihi al-ṭāqati sirwālayni wa-khayyiṭhumā al-yawma hādhā
sentences.l: and said to him: My lady says to you: Cut-out for her from this length two trousers, and sew them-both the day this.
sentences.i: and said to him, "My lady says to you: Cut her two pairs of trousers from this piece, and sew them today."
sentences.n: اليوم هذا ("the day this") is the Middle Arabic order, with the demonstrative after a noun that already has its article; classical would be هذا اليوم. It means "this very day".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً سَلِّمِي عَلَيْهَا السَّلَامَ الْكَثِيرَ وَقُولِي لَهَا عَبْدُكِ مُنْقَادٌ لِأَمْرِكِ فَا حْكُمِي عَلَيْهَا بِمَا شِئْتِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan sallimī ʿalayhā al-salāma al-kathīra wa-qūlī lahā ʿabduki munqādun li-amriki fa-ḥkumī ʿalayhā bi-mā shiʾti
sentences.l: And he said to-her: Hearing and obedience. Give-greeting upon her the greeting the abundant, and say to her: Your slave is submissive to your command; so rule upon her by what you wished.
sentences.i: He said to her, "With hearing and obedience. Give her my warmest greetings, and tell her: Your servant is at your command; so ordain for him whatever you will."
sentences.n: The words after قولي لها are addressed through the maid to the lady, hence the feminine -ki in عبدك, لأمرك, شئت. فا حكمي is printed as two words; it is fa-ḥkumī, "so rule!" (the imperative's alif drops after fa-). عليها is printed with the third-person pronoun, where "over me" (عليّ) would be expected; I keep what is printed and translate by the sense.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ شَرَعَ فِى التَّفْصِيلِ وَاجْتَهَدَ فِي خِيَاطَةِ السِّرْوَالَيْنِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu sharaʿa fī al-tafṣīli wa-ijtahada fī khiyāṭati al-sirwālayni
sentences.l: Then indeed-he began in the cutting-out and exerted-himself in the sewing of-the-two-trousers.
sentences.i: Then he set about the cutting, and worked with all his diligence at sewing the trousers.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ سَاعَةٍ تَطَلَّعَتْ لَهُ مِنَ الشُّبَّاكِ وَسَلَّمَتْ عَلَيْهِ بِالْإِيمَاءِ وَهِى تَارَةً تَغُضُّ طَرْفَهَا وَتَارَةً تَتَبَسَّمُ فِي وَجْهِهِ وَهُوَ يَظُنُّ أَنَّهُ سَيَظْفَرُ بِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda sāʿatin taṭallaʿat lahu min al-shubbāki wa-sallamat ʿalayhi bi-al-īmāʾi wa-hiya tāratan taghuḍḍu ṭarfahā wa-tāratan tatabassamu fī wajhihi wa-huwa yaẓunnu annahu sa-yaẓfaru bihā
sentences.l: And after an hour she looked-out for him from the lattice-window, and gave-greeting upon him by the signing, and she (was) at-one-time lowering her glance, and at-another-time smiling in his face, and he thinks that he will win her.
sentences.i: After an hour she looked out at him from the lattice and greeted him with a sign, now lowering her eyes, now smiling at him, while he fancied that he would win her.
sentences.n: شباك shubbāk is a lattice window. الإيماء al-īmāʾ is signalling with a nod or gesture. تارة ... وتارة is "now ... now". The verb ظفر takes بـ for the person won (ẓafira bi-: "to get the better of, to win").

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا غَابَتْ عَنْهُ وَجَاءَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ إِلَيْهِ فَسَلَّمَ إِلَيْهَا السِّرْوَالَيْنِ فَأَخَذَتْهُمَا وَانْصَرَفَتْ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā ghābat ʿanhu wa-jāʾati al-jāriyatu ilayhi fa-sallama ilayhā al-sirwālayni fa-akhadhathumā wa-inṣarafat
sentences.l: Then indeed-she vanished from him, and the girl came to him, and he handed to-her the two trousers, and she took them-both and went-off.
sentences.i: Then she withdrew from him, and the maid came to him; he handed her the two pairs of trousers, and she took them and went away.

sentences.t: وَلَمَّا أَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ انْطَرَحَ عَلَى فِرَاشِهِ وَبَاتَ يَتَقَلَّبُ إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-lammā aqbala al-laylu inṭaraḥa ʿalā firāshihi wa-bāta yataqallabu ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: And when the night approached, he threw-himself on his bed and spent-the-night tossing until the morning.
sentences.i: When night fell he flung himself down on his bed and lay tossing and turning till morning.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ قَامَ وَجَلَسَ فِي مَكَانِهِ فَجَاءَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ إِلَيْهِ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ إِنَّ مَوْلَايَ يَدْعُوكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa qāma wa-jalasa fī makānihi fa-jāʾati al-jāriyatu ilayhi wa-qālat lahu inna mawlāya yadʿūka
sentences.l: And when he reached-morning he rose and sat in his place, and the girl came to him and said to him: Indeed my master summons you.
sentences.i: In the morning he rose and sat down in his place, and the maid came to him and said, "My master is calling for you."

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ ذَلِكَ خَافَ خَوْفًا عَظِيمًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa dhālika khāfa khawfan ʿaẓīman
sentences.l: And when he heard that, he feared a fear great.
sentences.i: When he heard this, he was seized with great fear.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا شَعَرَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ بِخَوْفِهِ قَالَتْ لَهُ لَابَأْسَ عَلَيْكَ مَا هُنَاكَ إِلَّالِخَيْرٍ فَقَدْ جَعَلَتْ سِتِّي بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَ سَيِّدِي مَعْرِفَةً
sentences.tr: fa-lammā shaʿarati al-jāriyatu bi-khawfihi qālat lahu lā baʾsa ʿalayka mā hunāka illā li-khayrin fa-qad jaʿalat sittī baynaka wa-bayna sayyidī maʿrifatan
sentences.l: And when the girl became-aware of his fear, she said to him: No harm upon you; there is nothing there but for good; for my lady has made between you and my master an acquaintance.
sentences.i: When the maid saw his fear, she said, "You have nothing to fear. There is nothing here but good: my lady has made you and my master acquainted."
sentences.n: لابأس and إلالخير are each run together in the print (lā baʾsa, illā li-khayr). لا بأس عليك is the usual reassurance, "no harm to you". شعر بـ takes bi- for what is perceived (shaʿara bi-: "to be aware of").

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ الرَّجُلُ فَرَحًا عَظِيمًا ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ مَعَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa al-rajulu faraḥan ʿaẓīman thumma dhahaba maʿahā
sentences.l: And the man rejoiced a rejoicing great, then went with her.
sentences.i: The man was overjoyed, and he went off with her.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ عَلَى سَيِّدِهَا زَوْجِ سِتِّهَا قَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ فَرَدَّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhala ʿalā sayyidihā zawji sittihā qabbala al-arḍa fa-radda ʿalayhi al-salāma
sentences.l: And when he entered upon her master, the husband of her lady, he kissed the ground, and he returned to-him the greeting.
