sentences.i: When he went in to her master, her lady's husband, he kissed the ground before him, and the man returned his greeting.
sentences.n: Kissing the ground is the gesture of deference to a superior. ستها is sittihā, "her lady" (the maid's mistress): the master of the house is the husband of the lady who has been signalling from the window.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَاوَلَهُ ثِيَابًا كَثِيرَةً وَقَالَ لَهُ فَصِّلْ لِي مِنْ هَذَا وَخَيِّطْهُ قَمِيصًا
sentences.tr: thumma nāwalahu thiyāban kathīratan wa-qāla lahu faṣṣil lī min hādhā wa-khayyiṭhu qamīṣan
sentences.l: Then he handed him clothes many, and said to him: Cut-out for me from this, and sew it, a shirt.
sentences.i: Then he handed him a great quantity of cloth and said, "Cut me a shirt from this and sew it."
sentences.n: ثياب here means lengths of cloth rather than finished garments; the print has the singular قميصا ("a shirt"), though the tailor ends up cutting twenty.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَخِي سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً وَلَمْ يَزَلْ يُفَصِّلُ حَتَّى فَصَّلَ عِشْرِينَ قَمِيصًا إِلَى وَقْتِ الْعِشَاءِ فَلَمْ يَذُقْ طَعَامًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla akhī samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan wa-lam yazal yufaṣṣilu ḥattā faṣṣala ʿishrīna qamīṣan ilā waqti al-ʿishāʾi fa-lam yadhuq ṭaʿāman
sentences.l: And my brother said: Hearing and obedience; and he did not cease cutting-out until he had cut-out twenty shirt, until the time of-the-evening-meal; and he did not taste food.
sentences.i: My brother said, "With hearing and obedience," and he went on cutting until he had cut out twenty shirts, working on to the evening meal, and he never tasted a bite.
sentences.n: عشرين قميصا is the classical construction: after the numerals 11 to 99 the counted noun is singular and accusative ("twenty shirt"). العشاء is the evening, and the evening meal.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ كَمْ يَكُونُ لِذَلِكَ أُجْرَةً فَقَالَ لَهُ عِشْرُونَ دِرْهَمًا
sentences.tr: thumma qāla lahu kam yakūnu li-dhālika ujratan fa-qāla lahu ʿishrūna dirhaman
sentences.l: Then he said to him: How much will be for that, as wage? And he said to him: Twenty dirhams.
sentences.i: Then he asked him, "What will the wage be for that?" and the answer came, "Twenty dirhams."
sentences.n: The print does not say who speaks; the sequel (the husband calling for the money, the tailor holding his tongue) suggests that the husband asks and the tailor names the price. كم takes its counted noun in the accusative: ujratan.

sentences.t: فَزَعَقَ زَوْجُهَا عَلَى الْجَارِيَةِ وَقَالَ هَاتِي عِشْرِينَ دِرْهَمًا
sentences.tr: fa-zaʿaqa zawjuhā ʿalā al-jāriyati wa-qāla hāti ʿishrīna dirhaman
sentences.l: And her husband shouted at the girl and said: Bring twenty dirhams.
sentences.i: Her husband called out to the maid, "Bring twenty dirhams!"
sentences.n: هاتي hātī is the feminine imperative "bring, give". The lady's husband gives the order as soon as the sum is named.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَتَكَلَّمْ أَخِي فَأَشَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ الصَّبِيَّةُ يَعْنِي لَا تَأْخُذْ مِنْهُ شَيْأً
sentences.tr: fa-lam yatakallam akhī fa-ashārat ilayhi al-ṣabiyyatu yaʿnī lā taʾkhudh minhu shayʾan
sentences.l: And my brother did not speak, and the young-woman signalled to him, meaning: Do not take from him anything.
sentences.i: My brother said nothing, and the young woman signalled to him, meaning, "Take nothing from him."
sentences.n: الصبية is the lady herself (a young woman), not the maid. يعني is the narrator's gloss on her sign. The print writes شيأ with the hamza on the alif seat, shayʾ.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ مَا آخُذُ مِنْكَ شَيْأً وَأَخَذَ الْخِيَاطَةَ وَخَرَجَ إِى بَرٍّ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla wa-Allāhi mā ākhudhu minka shayʾan wa-akhadha al-khiyāṭata wa-kharaja ilā barrin
sentences.l: And he said: By God, I take from you nothing; and he took the sewing and went out to an outside.
sentences.i: And he said, "By God, I will take nothing from you." Then he took his sewing and went outside.
sentences.n: اى برّ is, I think, إلى with its lām missing in the print (ilā barr, "out, into the open"); I point the letters as printed, with a kasra on the alif, and read it ilā. The print has a shadda on the ر of برّ, which is kept. ما آخذ with the present tense is a firm refusal, "I will not take".

sentences.t: وَكَانَ أَخِي مُحْتَاجًا إِلَى فَلْسٍ وَبَقِيَ لَهُ ثَلٰثَةُ أَيَّامٍ لَايَأْ كُلُ وَلَا يَشْرَبُ إِلَّا الْقَلِيلَ مِنِ اجْتِهَادِهِ فِي تِلْكَ الْخِيَاطَةِ الَّتِي لَهُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna akhī muḥtājan ilā falsin wa-baqiya lahu thalāthatu ayyāmin lāyaʾ kulu wa-lā yashrabu illā al-qalīla min ijtihādihi fī tilka al-khiyāṭati allatī lahum
sentences.l: And my brother was needy to a fils, and there remained to him three days, not eating and not drinking except the little from his exertion in that sewing which was theirs.
sentences.i: My brother was in need of a single copper coin; for three days he had neither eaten nor drunk, save for the little his labour brought him at the tailoring they gave him.
sentences.n: The brother is one of the barber's six brothers; the barber is still telling the Caliph the tale. A fils is the smallest copper coin. The print runs لايا كل with a stray space; it is pointed as lā yaʾkulu ("he does not eat"), the hamza carried by the alif of يا. The bare clause after "three days" ("not eating and not drinking") is circumstantial: Arabic needs no "during which".

sentences.t: فَأَتَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ أَيْشْ عَمِلْتَ فَقَالَ فَرَغُوا فَأَخَذَهُمْ وَأَتَي إِلَيْهِمْ بِهَا وَسَلَّمَ إِى زَوْجِهَا الثِّيَابَ وَانْصَرَفَ مِنْ سَاعَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-atati al-jāriyatu wa-qālat lahu ayshi ʿamilta fa-qāla faraghū fa-akhadhahum wa-atā ilayhim bihā wa-sallama ilā zawjihā al-thiyāba wa-inṣarafa min sāʿatihi
sentences.l: And came the girl and said to him: What did-you-do? And he said: They-have-finished. And he took them and came to them with it, and handed to her husband the garments, and went-off from his hour.
sentences.i: The girl came and asked him, "What have you done?" "They are finished," he said. He took the garments, brought them back with the finished work, handed them to her husband, and left at once.
sentences.n: أَيْشْ is the colloquial contraction of أَيُّ شَيْءٍ, "what?". The print writes أتي with a yā where Classical has the alif maqṣūra (atā, "he came"); it is pointed as atā. The following اى is the print's spelling of إلى with the lām missing; it is pointed ilā. The "it" in بِهَا is the finished sewing (feminine الخياطة), not the garments, which are plural and are taken as "them". مِنْ سَاعَتِهِ, "from his hour", means "at that very moment".

sentences.t: وَكَانَتِ الصَّبِيَّةُ قَدْ عَرَّفَتْ زَوْجَهَا بِحَالِ أَخِي وَأَخِي لَا يَعْلَمُ ذٰلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-kānati al-ṣabiyyatu qad ʿarrafat zawjahā bi-ḥāli akhī wa-akhī lā yaʿlamu dhālika
sentences.l: And the young-woman had informed her husband with the state of my brother, and my brother not knowing that.
sentences.i: Now the young woman had told her husband of my brother's plight, though my brother knew nothing of it.
sentences.n: عَرَّفَ بِـ is "to make known (a matter) to someone"; the person told is the direct object (زَوْجَهَا), the thing told is introduced by بِـ.

sentences.t: وَاتَّفَقَتْ هِىَ وَزَوْجُهَا عَلَى اسْتِعْمَالِ أَخِي فِى الْخِيَاطَةِ بِلَا شَئٍْ وَيَضْحَكُونَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-ittafaqat hiya wa-zawjuhā ʿalā istiʿmāli akhī fī al-khiyāṭati bi-lā shayʾin wa-yaḍḥakūna ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And agreed she and her husband upon the employing of my brother in the sewing with-no thing, and they laugh upon him.
sentences.i: She and her husband agreed to put my brother to work at the tailoring for nothing, and to make a laughing-stock of him.
sentences.n: The print has شي without hamza; it is read shayʾ, so بِلَا شَيْئٍ is "for nothing". ضَحِكَ عَلَى is "to laugh at, to make a fool of". The last verb, يَضْحَكُونَ, is a bare present continuing the sentence: "and (so as to) laugh at him".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ أَتَى إِلَى الدُّكَّانِ فَأَتَتْ إِلَيْهِ الْجَارِيَةُ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ كَلِّمْ سَيِّدِي فَذَهَبَ مَعَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu atā ilā al-dukkāni fa-atat ilayhi al-jāriyatu wa-qālat lahu kallim sayyidī fa-dhahaba maʿahā
sentences.l: And when the morning became-morning, he came to the shop, and came to him the girl and said to him: Speak-to my master. And he went with her.
sentences.i: When morning broke he came to his shop, and the girl came to him and said, "Come and speak to my master." So he went with her.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَصَلَ إِلَيْهِ قَالَ لَهُ أُرِيدُ مِنْكَ أَنْ تُفَصِّلَ لِي خَمْسَ فَرَجِيَّاتٍ فَفَصَّلَ لَهُ وَأَخَذَ الثِّيَابَ مَعَهُ وَانْصَرَفَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waṣala ilayhi qāla lahu urīdu minka an tufaṣṣila lī khamsa farajiyyātin fa-faṣṣala lahu wa-akhadha al-thiyāba maʿahu wa-inṣarafa
sentences.l: And when he arrived to him, he said to him: I want from you that you cut-out for me five farajiyyas. And he cut-out for him, and took the cloth with him, and went-off.
sentences.i: When he reached the man, the man said to him, "I want you to cut out five robes for me." He cut them out, took the cloth with him, and went away.
sentences.n: فَرَجِيَّة (farajiyya) is a long, loose outer robe with wide sleeves, worn by scholars and townsmen. Cutting out (تَفْصِيل) is the tailor's first stage, sewing (خِيَاطَة) the second.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ خَيَّطَ تِلْكَ الْفَرَجِيَّاتِ وَمَضَى بِهَا إِلَيْهِ فَاسْتَحْسَنَ خِيَاطَتَهُ وَادَّعَى بِكِيسٍ فِيهِ دَرَاهِمُ وَمَدَّيَدَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu khayyaṭa tilka al-farajiyyāti wa-maḍā bihā ilayhi fa-istaḥsana khiyāṭatahu wa-iddaʿā bi-kīsin fīhi darāhimu wa-maddayadahu
sentences.l: Then he sewed those farajiyyas and went with them to him; and he found-good his sewing, and called for a purse in which (were) dirhams, and stretched-his-hand.
sentences.i: Then he sewed the robes and carried them back to the man, who admired his work, called for a purse of dirhams, and stretched out his hand to pay.
sentences.n: وَادَّعَى بِكِيسٍ: I take this as "he called for a purse" (ادَّعَى بِـ, Form VIII of دعا, is "to call for"); the usual meaning of ادَّعَى, "to claim", would make no sense here. The print has run ومد يده together as ومديده; it is pointed as one word, wa-madda yadahu.

sentences.t: فَأَشَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ الصَّبِيَّةُ مِنْ خَلْفِ زَوْجِهَا أَنْ لَاتَأْخُذَ شَيْئًا
sentences.tr: fa-ashārat ilayhi al-ṣabiyyatu min khalfi zawjihā an lātaʾkhudha shayʾan
sentences.l: And signalled to him the young-woman, from behind her husband, that (he should) not take a thing.
sentences.i: But the young woman, from behind her husband's back, signalled to him not to take anything.
sentences.n: The print runs لا تأخذ together as لاتاخذ.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِلرَّجُلِ يَا سَيِّدِي لَاتَعْجَلْ فَالزَّمَانُ مُوَانِي وَخَرَجَ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ وَهُوَ أَذَلُّ مِنْ حِمَارٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla li-al-rajuli yā sayyidī lātaʿjal fa-al-zamānu muwānī wa-kharaja min ʿindihi wa-huwa adhallu min ḥimārin
sentences.l: And he said to the man: O my master, do-not hasten, for the time (is) accommodating. And he went-out from with-him, and he (was) more-abject than a donkey.
sentences.i: So he said to the man, "My lord, there is no hurry; time is kind." And he left him, more wretched than a donkey.
sentences.n: مُوَانِي is obscure. I read it as the active participle of وَانَى (Form III, "to be gentle with, to be accommodating"), so "time is accommodating, there is time"; the word may be corrupt. He refuses the money because the young woman's signal told him to, and covers the refusal with a courtesy. أَذَلُّ مِنْ حِمَارٍ, "more abject than a donkey", is a proverbial comparison.

sentences.t: وَقَدِ اجْتَمَعَ عَلَيْهِ خَمْسَةُ أَشْيَاءَ عِشْقٌ وَإِفْلَاسٌ وَجُوعٌ وَعُرْىٌ وَتَعَبٌ وَإِنَّمَا هُوَ يُشَجِّعُ نَفْسَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qadi ijtamaʿa ʿalayhi khamsatu ashyāʾa ʿishqun wa-iflāsun wa-jūʿun wa-ʿuryun wa-taʿabun wa-innamā huwa yushajjiʿu nafsahu
sentences.l: And there had gathered upon him five things: passion, and bankruptcy, and hunger, and nakedness, and weariness; and only he (was) heartening his self.
sentences.i: Five afflictions had piled upon him: love, penury, hunger, nakedness, and exhaustion; and still he went on putting heart into himself.
sentences.n: The five things are listed with a wa- before each, without commas. عِشْق is passionate love, here for the girl. The print writes عرى with the yā-shaped ى; it is read ʿurī, "nakedness" (that is, threadbare clothes).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ أَخِي مِنْ جَمِيعِ أَشْغَالِهِمْ فَبَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ عَمِلُوا عَلَيْهِ حِيلَةً وَزَوَّجُوهُ بِجَارِيَتِهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha akhī min jamīʿi ashghālihim fa-baʿda dhālika ʿamilū ʿalayhi ḥīlatan wa-zawwajūhu bi-jāriyatihim
sentences.l: And when my brother had finished from all their jobs, then after that they made upon him a trick, and married him with their girl.
sentences.i: When my brother had finished all their work, they contrived a trick against him: they married him to their own slave-girl.
sentences.n: The second fa- (فَبَعْدَ) opens the main clause after the lammā-clause, as often in Middle Arabic. زَوَّجَهُ بِـ puts the bride after بِـ (Classical would say زَوَّجَهُ إِيَّاهَا); the bi- marks the woman he is wed to.

sentences.t: وَفِى اللَّيْلَةِ الَّتِى أَرَادَ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ عَلَيْهَا قَالُوا لَهُ بِتِ اللَّيْلَةَ فِى الطَّاحُونِ إِلَى غَدٍ يَكُونُ خَيْرًا
sentences.tr: wa-fī al-laylati allatī arāda an yadkhula ʿalayhā qālū lahu biti al-layla fī al-ṭāḥūni ilā ghadin yakūnu khayran
sentences.l: And in the night which he wanted that he enter upon her, they said to him: Spend-the-night the night in the mill; until tomorrow it will be good.
sentences.i: And on the night he was to go in to her, they said to him, "Spend this night in the mill; by tomorrow all will be well."
sentences.n: دَخَلَ عَلَى is "to go in to" a bride, to consummate the marriage. بِتِ is the imperative of بَاتَ, "to spend the night", shortened by the long vowel dropping before the closed syllable and then given a linking kasra before اللَّيْلَةَ. إِلَى غَدٍ يَكُونُ خَيْرًا: "by tomorrow it will be good", a bare promise that sounds kind and is a lie.

sentences.t: فَا عْتَقَدَ أَخِي أَنَّهُ صَحِيحٌ فَبَاتَ فِى الطَّاحُونِ وَحْدَهُ وَرَاحَ زَوْجُ الصَّبِيَّةِ غَمَزَ الطَّحَّانَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-iʿtaqada akhī annahu ṣaḥīḥun fa-bāta fī al-ṭāḥūni waḥdahu wa-rāḥa zawju al-ṣabiyyati ghamaza al-ṭaḥḥāna ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And thought my brother that it (was) sound; and he spent-the-night in the mill alone; and went the husband of the young-woman (and) winked the miller upon him,
sentences.i: My brother believed it was all in earnest, and so he spent the night in the mill alone. Meanwhile the girl's husband went off and gave the miller a wink about him,
sentences.n: The print has a stray space in فا عتقد (the alif of the fa- belongs to the verb, i‘taqada); I keep the printed spacing. رَاحَ غَمَزَ, "he went (and) winked", strings two verbs without wa-, a colloquial habit. غَمَزَ عَلَيْهِ is "to give a sign about someone", here a tip-off. The print marks the shadda on the ط of الطّحان; the one on the ح is ours.

sentences.t: حَتَّى أَنَّهُ يُدَوِّرُهُ فِى الطَّاحُونِ
sentences.tr: ḥattā annahu yudawwiruhu fī al-ṭāḥūni
sentences.l: until that he turn-him-round in the mill.
sentences.i: so that he would set him circling round the mill.
sentences.n: حَتَّى أَنَّهُ with a present verb: "so that he" (Classical would take the subjunctive, حَتَّى يُدَوِّرَهُ). The mill is turned by an animal walking in a circle, so the brother is to be made to do the ox's work.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ الطَّحَّانُ نِصْفَ اللَّيْلِ وَجَعَلَ يَقُولُ هٰذَا الثَّوْرُ بَطَلَ وَوَقَفَ وَلَابَقِيَ يَدُورُ فِي هٰذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَالْقَمْحُ عِنْدَنَا كَثِيرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhala ʿalayhi al-ṭaḥḥānu niṣfa al-layli wa-jaʿala yaqūlu hādhā al-thawru baṭala wa-waqafa wa-lābaqiya yadūru fī hādhihi al-laylati wa-al-qamḥu ʿindanā kathīrun
sentences.l: And entered upon him the miller (at) half-the-night, and began saying: This ox has ceased and stopped, and no-longer circles in this night, and the wheat with-us (is) much.
sentences.i: At midnight the miller came in to him and began to say, "This ox has given up and stopped; it won't go round tonight, and we have a great deal of wheat."
sentences.n: The miller speaks as if the brother were his ox. بَطَلَ is "to cease work, be idle". وَلَابَقِيَ يَدُورُ (printed as one word), "and he no longer goes round", uses baqiya with a present verb for "no longer", a colloquial turn. نِصْفَ اللَّيْلِ is an accusative of time.

sentences.t: وَنَزَلَ عَلَى الطَّاحُونِ مَلَأَ الْقَادُوسَ قَمْحًا وَقَصَدَ أَخِي
sentences.tr: wa-nazala ʿalā al-ṭāḥūni malaʾa al-qādūsa qamḥan wa-qaṣada akhī
sentences.l: And he went-down upon the mill, filled the hopper (with) wheat, and made-for my brother.
sentences.i: He went down to the mill, filled the hopper with wheat, and made for my brother.
sentences.n: القَادُوس (qādūs) is a bucket or pot, from Greek; in a mill I take it to be the hopper that feeds the grain to the stone. ملأ is printed with the precomposed أ in the edition.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ فِي يَدِهِ حَبْلٌ فَرَبَطَ رَقَبَتَهُ وَقَالَ هَيَّا دُرْ عَلَى الْقَمْحِ مَا مُرَادُكَ إِلَّا تَأْكُلُ تَخْرَاً وَتَبُولُ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna fī yadihi ḥablun fa-rabaṭa raqabatahu wa-qāla hayyā dur ʿalā al-qamḥi mā murāduka illā taʾkulu takhrā wa-tabūlu
sentences.l: And there was in his hand a rope, and he tied his neck and said: Come-on, circle upon the wheat! What (is) your desire except you eat, you shit, and you piss?
sentences.i: He had a rope in his hand; he tied it round my brother's neck and cried, "Come on, go round on the wheat! All you want is to eat, and shit, and piss!"
sentences.n: هَيَّا is the cry used to start an animal moving. The print marks a tanwīn fatḥa on the alif of تخرا; I take it as a verb, takhrā, "you shit" (colloquial, from خَرِئَ/خَرَى), and the tanwīn as a printer's oddity. It is obscure and may be corrupt. The sentence is the miller's taunt at the "ox": it does nothing but eat and void itself.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَخَذَ سَوْطًا فِي يَدِهِ وَضَرَبَهُ بِهِ وَأَخِي يَبْكِي وَيَصِيحُ فَلَمْ يَجِدْ لَهُ مُغِيثًا
sentences.tr: thumma akhadha sawṭan fī yadihi wa-ḍarabahu bihi wa-akhī yabkī wa-yaṣīḥu fa-lam yajid lahu mughīthan
sentences.l: Then he took a whip in his hand and struck him with it, while my brother weeps and cries-out, and he did not find for himself a helper.
sentences.i: Then he took a whip in his hand and beat him with it, while my brother wept and screamed, and found no one to help him.

sentences.t: وَالْقَمْحُ يَنْطَحِنُ إِلَى قَرِيبِ الصُّبْحِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-qamḥu yanṭaḥinu ilā qarībi al-ṣubḥi
sentences.l: And the wheat (was) being-ground until near the morning.
sentences.i: And the wheat went on being ground until nearly dawn.
sentences.n: يَنْطَحِنُ is Form VII, "to get ground", the passive-reflexive of طَحَنَ.

sentences.t: فَجَاءَ صَاحِبُ الدَّارِ فَرَأَى أَخِي مُعَلَّقًا عَلَى الْخَشَبَةِ وَمَضَى
sentences.tr: fa-jāʾa ṣāḥibu al-dāri fa-raʾā akhī muʿallaqan ʿalā al-khashabati wa-maḍā
sentences.l: And came the master of the house, and saw my brother hung upon the wood, and went-off.
sentences.i: Then the master of the house came, saw my brother hanging from the beam, and went away.
sentences.n: الْخَشَبَة, "the piece of wood", is presumably the sweep of the mill to which he was harnessed. The master of the house is the husband, who has come to look and leaves again without a word.

sentences.t: وَجَاءَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ إِلَيْهِ بَاكِرَ النَّهَارِ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَعِزُّ عَلَىَّ مَاجَرَى لَكَ أَنَا وَسِتِّي قَدْ حَمَلْنَا هَمَّكَ
sentences.tr: wa-jāʾati al-jāriyatu ilayhi bākira al-nahāri wa-qālat lahu yaʿizzu ʿalayya mājarā laka anā wa-sittī qad ḥamalnā hammaka
sentences.l: And came the girl to him early (in) the day and said to him: It is hard upon me what happened to you. I and my lady have carried your worry.
sentences.i: Early the next morning the girl came to him and said, "It grieves me what has happened to you. My lady and I have taken your trouble upon ourselves."
sentences.n: يَعِزُّ عَلَيَّ is "it pains me". The print has عَلَى in the form على with no shadda; it must be read ʿalayya, "upon me". ما جرى is printed as one word, mājarā. سِتِّي is sittī, "my lady" (ستّ, colloquial for سيّدة).

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ لِسَانٌ يَرُدُّ جَوَابًا مِنْ شِدَّةِ الضَّرْبِ وَالتَّعَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yakun lahu lisānun yaruddu jawāban min shiddati al-ḍarbi wa-al-taʿabi
sentences.l: And there was not to him a tongue (to) return an answer, from the severity of the beating and the weariness.
sentences.i: He had no tongue left to answer her, such was the force of the beating and the weariness.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ أَخِي أَتَى إِلَى مَنْزِلِهِ وَإِذَا بِالْمُعَلِّمِ الَّذِي كَتَبَ الْكِتَابَ قَدْ جَاءَ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma inna akhī atā ilā manzilihi wa-idhā bi-al-muʿallimi alladhī kataba al-kitāba qad jāʾa wa-sallama ʿalayhi wa-qāla lahu
sentences.l: Then my brother came to his lodging, and behold, the master who wrote the writing had come and greeted him and said to him:
sentences.i: Then my brother went home, and there was the master who had drawn up the marriage contract, come to greet him; and he said,
sentences.n: وَإِذَا بِـ: after idhā of surprise the bi- only marks what appears ("and behold, the master..."). كَتَبَ الْكِتَابَ, "to write the writing", is the idiom for drawing up a marriage contract.

sentences.t: حَيَّاكَ اللَّهُ هٰذَا وَجْهُ النَّعِيمِ وَاللَّهِ لَالِ وَالْعِنَاقُ مِنَ الْعِشَاءِ الِي الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: ḥayyāka Allāhu hādhā wajhu al-naʿīmi wa-Allāhi lāli wa-al-ʿināqu min al-ʿishāʾi ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: May God give-you-life! This (is) the face of bliss! And by God, lāl, and the embracing from the evening to the morning!
sentences.i: "God keep you! Here is the face of bliss! By God, such nights, and embracing from nightfall till dawn!"
sentences.n: The master teases him. لال is obscure; I point it lāli and guess it is لَيَالٍ, "nights", with the yā lost in the print, which is how the translation takes it. The print has الي for إلى. حَيَّاكَ اللَّهُ, "may God give you life", is a greeting.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَخِي لَا سَلَّمَ اللَّهُ الْكَاذِبَ يَا أَلْفَ قَرْنَانٍ وَاللَّهِ مَا جِئْتُ إِلَّا طَحْنَ مَوْضِعِ الثَّوْرِ إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu akhī lā sallama Allāhu al-kādhiba yā alfa qarnānin wa-Allāhi mā jiʾtu illā ṭaḥna mawḍiʿi al-thawri ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: And said to him my brother: May God not keep-safe the liar! O thousand of cuckold! By God, I did not come except (to) the grinding of the place of the ox until the morning.
sentences.i: My brother answered, "May God not preserve the liar! You thousand-fold cuckold! By God, all I got was grinding in the ox's place till morning!"
sentences.n: قَرْنَان (qarnān) is a man who tolerates his wife's lovers, a cuckold; "a thousand of cuckold" is a stock insult. ما جئت إلا طحن is obscure: I read ṭaḥna as an accusative verbal noun, "I came (to nothing) but grinding"; the sense is clear even if the grammar is loose. The print has no mark on جئت beyond the ئ.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ حَدِّثْنِي بِحَدِيثِكَ فَحَدَّثَهُ أَخِي بِمَا وَقَعَ لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu ḥaddithnī bi-ḥadīthika fa-ḥaddathahu akhī bi-mā waqaʿa lahu
sentences.l: And he said to him: Tell-me with your tale. And my brother told him with what had befallen him.
sentences.i: "Tell me your story," said the master, and my brother told him all that had befallen him.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ مَا وَافَقَ نَجْمُكَ نَجْمَهَا وَلٰكِنْ إِذَا شِئْتَ أُغَيِّرُلَكَ ذٰلِكَ الْكِتَابَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu mā wāfaqa najmuka najmahā wa-lākin idhā shiʾta ughayyirulaka dhālika al-kitāba
sentences.l: And he said to him: Your star did not agree with her star; but if you wish, I (will) change-for-you that writing.
sentences.i: He said, "Your star was not matched with hers; but if you wish, I will alter that contract for you."
sentences.n: Stars are the usual reckoning of compatibility. The print joins اغير لك as اغيرلك, pointed here as one word, ughayyiru laka. "Change the contract" means to dissolve or rewrite the marriage.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ انْظُرْ إِنْ بَقِيَ لَكَ حِيلَةٌ أُخْرَى ثُمَّ تَرَكَهُ وَأَتَى إِلَى مَكَانِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu unẓur in baqiya laka ḥīlatun ukhrā thumma tarakahu wa-atā ilā makānihi
sentences.l: And he said to him: Look whether there remains to you another trick. Then he left him and came to his place.
sentences.i: He answered, "See whether you have any other trick left." Then he left him and went back to his place,
sentences.n: The print does not say who speaks the first sentence; I take it as the brother, answering the offer to cancel by asking for one more chance of a stratagem. This is a guess.

sentences.t: يَنْظُرُ أَحَدًا يَأْتِي إِلَيْهِ بِشُغْلٍ يَتَقَوَّتُ مِنْهُ وَإِذَا هُوَ بِالْجَارِيَةِ قَدْ أَتَتْ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: yanẓuru aḥadan yaʾtī ilayhi bi-shughlin yataqawwatu minhu wa-idhā huwa bi-al-jāriyati qad atat ilayhi
sentences.l: looking (for) someone (to) come to him with work (from which) he might-sustain-himself; and behold, he (was) with the girl: she had come to him.
sentences.i: watching for anyone who might bring him a job to live on; and all at once there was the girl, come to him again.
sentences.n: يَتَقَوَّتُ مِنْهُ is "to keep oneself alive on it" (from قُوت, bare sustenance). The opening verb is a circumstantial clause attached to the end of the last sentence.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لَهُ كَلِّمْ سِتِّي فَقَالَ لَهَا رُوحِي يَابِنْتَ الْحَلَالِ مَا بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ سِتِّكِ مُعَامَلَةٌ فَرَاحَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ وَأَعْلَمَتْ سِتَّهَا بِذٰلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahu kallim sittī fa-qāla lahā rūḥī yābinta al-ḥalāli mā baynī wa-bayna sittiki muʿāmalatun fa-rāḥati al-jāriyatu wa-aʿlamat sittahā bi-dhālika
sentences.l: And she said to him: Speak-to my lady. And he said to her: Go, O daughter of the lawful, there is not between me and your lady any dealing. And the girl went and informed her lady of that.
sentences.i: She said, "Come and speak to my lady." "Be off with you, my good girl," he said, "there is nothing between me and your mistress." The girl went and told her mistress.
sentences.n: بِنْتَ الْحَلَالِ, "daughter of the lawful", is a familiar way of addressing a girl, "good girl". يا بنت is printed as one word. مُعَامَلَة is "dealings, business".

sentences.t: فَمَا دَرَي أَخِي إِلَّا وَهِيَ قَدْ طَلَعَتْ لَهُ مِنَ الرَّوْشَنِ وَهِيَ تَبْكِي وَتَقُولُ لَايْشْ يَا حَبِيبِي مَا بَقِيَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ مُعَامَلَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-mā darā akhī illā wa-hiya qad ṭalaʿat lahu min al-rawshani wa-hiya tabkī wa-taqūlu lāysh yā ḥabībī mā baqiya baynī wa-baynaka muʿāmalatun
sentences.l: And my brother did not know, but she had come-up to him from the bay-window, and she weeping and saying: Why, O my beloved? There has not remained between me and you any dealing?
sentences.i: My brother knew nothing until she had come up to him from the bay window, weeping, and saying, "Why, my love? Is there nothing left between you and me?"
sentences.n: فَمَا دَرَى ... إِلَّا, "he knew nothing until", means "suddenly". The print writes دري with a yā. الرَّوْشَن (rawshan) is a projecting window or balcony, from Persian rōzan. لايش is colloquial lēsh, "why", from لِأَيِّ شَيْءٍ.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَرُدَّ عَلَيْهَا جَوَابًا فَحَلَفَتْ لَهُ أَنَّ جَمِيعَ مَا وَقَعَ لَهُ فِي الطَّاحُونِ لَمْ يَكُنْ بِاخْتِيَارِهَا وَأَنَّهَا بَرِيئَةٌ مِنْ ذٰلِكَ الْأَمْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yarudda ʿalayhā jawāban fa-ḥalafat lahu anna jamīʿa mā waqaʿa lahu fī al-ṭāḥūni lam yakun bi-ikhtiyārihā wa-annahā barīʾatun min dhālika al-amri
sentences.l: And he did not return to her an answer; and she swore to him that all that had befallen him in the mill was not by her choice, and that she (was) innocent from that matter.
sentences.i: He gave her no answer, so she swore to him that all that had happened to him in the mill had been no choice of hers, and that she was innocent of the whole affair.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَأَخِي إِلَى حُسْنِهَا وَجَمَالِهَا وَسَمِعَ كَلَامَهَا ذَهَبَ عَنْهُ مَا حَصَلَ لَهُ وَقَبِلَ عُذْرَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓara akhī ilā ḥusnihā wa-jamālihā wa-samiʿa kalāmahā dhahaba ʿanhu mā ḥaṣala lahu wa-qabila ʿudhrahā
sentences.l: And when my brother looked at her beauty and her loveliness and heard her speech, there went from him what had come to him, and he accepted her excuse.
sentences.i: But when my brother looked at her beauty and her loveliness, and heard her words, all that he had suffered passed from him, and he accepted her excuse.
sentences.n: The print runs نظر أخي together as نظراخي; it is pointed as naẓara akhī. ذَهَبَ عَنْهُ, "went from him", means he forgot it.

sentences.t: وَفَرِحَ بِرُؤْيَتِهَا ثُمَّ سَلَّمَ عَلَيْهَا وَتَحَدَّثَ مَعَهَا وَجَلَسَ فِي خِيَاطَتِهِ مُدَّةً
sentences.tr: wa-fariḥa bi-ruʾyatihā thumma sallama ʿalayhā wa-taḥaddatha maʿahā wa-jalasa fī khiyāṭatihi muddatan
sentences.l: And he rejoiced at the seeing-of-her, then he greeted upon her, and he conversed with her, and he sat in his tailoring for a time.
sentences.i: He was glad to see her. He greeted her and talked with her, and then he sat down to his tailoring for a while.
sentences.n: This unit starts in the middle of a sentence: the lame man's brother, the tailor, has just accepted the young woman's excuse ("and he accepted her excuse"), and the verbs carry on from there. سَلَّمَ عَلَى is "to greet" (literally "to give peace upon").

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ جَاءَتْ لَهُ الْجَارِيَةُ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ تُسَلِّمُ عَلَيْكَ سَتِّي وَتَقُولُ لَكَ إنَّ زَوْجَهَا قَدْ عَزَمَ أنَّهُ يَبِيتُ عِنْدَ أصْلِ قَائِهِ اللَّيْلَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna baʿda dhālika jāʾat lahu al-jāriyatu wa-qālat lahu tusallimu ʿalayka sittī wa-taqūlu laka inna zawjahā qad ʿazama annahu yabītu ʿinda aṣli qāʾihi al-laylata
sentences.l: And when it was after that, the girl came to him, and she said to him: There greets upon you my lady, and she says to you: Indeed her husband has resolved that he will pass-the-night at the origin of his qāʾ(?), the night.
sentences.i: Some time after this, the maid came to him and said, "My lady sends you her greetings, and she bids me tell you that her husband has made up his mind to spend tonight at his kinsmen's house.
sentences.n: قَائِهِ is printed قائه, and I cannot identify it with confidence. اصل قائه ("the origin of his qāʾ") has no clear reading; a misprint for some word meaning "his family" or "his town" is likely, and the sense required by the story is simply that the husband will be away for the night. The idiomatic layer follows that sense; the pointing follows the print. تُسَلِّمُ عَلَيْكَ is the stock greeting-message formula, "she greets you". The quotation opened here by the maid carries on into the next unit.

sentences.t: فَإذَا مَضَى هُوَعِنْدَهُمْ تَكُونُ أنْتَ عِنْدَنَا وَتَبِيتُ مَعَ سِتِّى فِي الْعَيْشِ إلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā maḍā huwaʿindahum takūnu anta ʿindanā wa-tabītu maʿa sittī fī al-ʿayshi ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: So when he has gone, he at-their-place, you will be at our place, and you will pass-the-night with my lady in the life until the morning.
sentences.i: Once he has gone off to them, you will be with us, and you will spend the night with my lady in pleasure until morning."
sentences.n: The print runs هو and عندهم together (هوعندهم); it is pointed as one word, huwa + ʿindahum, "he is with them" or "he (being) at their place". The indicative تَكُونُ and تَبِيتُ stand for the future, as the main clause after فَإِذَا. فِي الْعَيْشِ, literally "in the life", means in easy living, in pleasure; the sexual sense is plain from the context.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ زَوْجُهَا قَدْ قَالَ لَهَا مَا يَكُونُ الْعَمَلُ فِي رُجُوعِهِ عَنْكَ فَقَالَتْ دَعْنِي أحْتَالَ عَلَيْهِ بِحِيلَةٍ أخْرَى وَأشَهِّرَهُ فِي هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ وَأخِي لَا يَعْلَمُ شَيْأً مِنْ كَيْدِ النِّسَاءِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna zawjuhā qad qāla lahā mā yakūnu al-ʿamalu fī rujūʿihi ʿanki fa-qālat daʿnī aḥtāla ʿalayhi bi-ḥīlatin ukhrā wa-ushahhirahu fī hādhihi al-madīnati wa-akhī lā yaʿlamu shayʾan min kaydi al-nisāʾi
sentences.l: And her husband had said to her: What will be the doing in his returning from you? So she said: Leave me, that I contrive against him with another trick and make-him-notorious in this city. And my brother knows not a thing of the guile of the women.
sentences.i: Now her husband had asked her, "What are we to do about his turning back from you?" and she had said, "Leave me to scheme against him with another trick, and I will make him a public disgrace in this city." And my brother knew nothing of the cunning of women.
sentences.n: This is the plotters' side of the story, told after the fact. Reading عَنْكَ as "from you" is my guess: the husband asks what is to be done now that the brother has turned back (or been turned back) from pursuing her; the Arabic does not say who is speaking to whom with perfect clarity. The print writes عنك with the masculine ـك although the husband is addressing his wife, who would be عنكِ; it is pointed as printed. After دَعْنِي the verbs are pointed with the subjunctive fatḥa, أَحْتَالَ and أُشَهِّرَهُ, since the print keeps the long alif; a classical jussive would be أَحْتَلْ. The shadda printed on the ه of واشهّره marks the intensive form شَهَّرَ, "to make notorious, parade in public".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ الْمَسَاءُ جَاءَتْهُ الْجَارِيَةُ وَأخَذَتْ أخِي رَجَعَتْ بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna al-masāʾu jāʾathu al-jāriyatu wa-akhadhat akhī rajaʿat bihi
sentences.l: And when it was the evening, the girl came to him, and she took my brother, she returned with him.
sentences.i: When evening came, the maid went to him, took my brother by the hand, and led him back with her.
sentences.n: وَأَخَذَتْ أَخِي رَجَعَتْ بِهِ is a run-on of two verbs with no conjunction between them, a common Middle Arabic way of describing one continuous action: "she took my brother, returned with him".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتِ الصَّبِيَّةُ بِأخِي قَالَتْ لَهُ وَاللَّهِ يَا سَيِّدِي إنِّي مُشْتَاقَةٌ إلَيْكَ كَثِيرًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾati al-ṣabiyyatu bi-akhī qālat lahu wa-Allāhi yā sayyidī innī mushtāqatun ilayka kathīran
sentences.l: And when the young woman saw (with) my brother, she said to him: By God, O my master, indeed I am longing to you much.
sentences.i: When the young woman saw my brother, she said to him, "By God, my lord, I have longed for you greatly."
sentences.n: The print has رات (rāt) with the hamza unwritten; it is pointed رَا^َتِ. The بِ in بِأَخِي is pleonastic with a verb of seeing here (or the sense is "saw herself with my brother"); it adds nothing in English. مُشْتَاقَةٌ إِلَيْكَ is "longing for you": اِشْتَاقَ إِلَى takes إِلَى.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ بِاللَّهِ عَجِّلِي بِقُبْلَةٍ قَبْلَ كُلِّ شَئٍ فَلَمْ يَتِمَّ كَلَامُهُ إلَّاوَحَضَرَ زَوْجُ الصَّبِيَّةِ مِنْ بَيْتٍ هُنَاكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla bi-Allāhi ʿajjilī bi-qublatin qabla kulli shayʾin fa-lam yatimma kalāmuhu illāwaḥaḍara zawju al-ṣabiyyati min baytin hunāka
sentences.l: So he said: By God, hasten with a kiss before every thing! And his speech had not completed except-and there was present the husband of the young woman from a house there.
sentences.i: And he said, "For God's sake, be quick with a kiss before anything else!" But he had hardly finished speaking when the young woman's husband appeared from a room nearby.
sentences.n: بِاللَّهِ here is an oath-like plea, "in God's name". عَجِّلِي is the feminine imperative, "hurry", and بِقُبْلَةٍ means "with a kiss" (hurry with it). The print runs الا and وحضر together; it is pointed إِلَّاوَحَضَرَ, the idiom "he had not finished speaking except that" (ما ... إلا و...), where the و introduces the sudden event. The print also omits the hamza in شيء, which is shown here as a hamza on the yāʾ. بَيْتٍ هُنَاكَ is "a house/room there": the husband was hiding close by, as the maid's message about his absence was a lie.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لِأخِي وَاللَّهِ لَا أُفَارِقُكَ إلَّا عِنْدَ صَاحِبِ الشُّرْطَةِ فَتَضَرَّعَ إلَيْهِ أخِي فَلَمْ يَسْمَعْهُ بَلْ حَمَلَهُ إلَى الْوَالِي
sentences.tr: wa-qāla li-akhī wa-Allāhi lā ufāriquka illā ʿinda ṣāḥibi al-shurṭati fa-taḍarraʿa ilayhi akhī fa-lam yasmaʿhu bal ḥamalahu ilā al-wālī
sentences.l: And he said to my brother: By God, I will not part from you except at the master-of-the-police. So my brother humbled himself to him, but he did not hear him; rather he carried him to the governor.
sentences.i: And he said to my brother, "By God, I will not let you go until I have you before the chief of police!" My brother begged him, but he would not listen, and carried him off to the governor.
sentences.n: The word written لا افارقك has no hamza on the alif in print; it is pointed لَا أُفَارِقُكَ, "I will not leave you". صَاحِبُ الشُّرْطَةِ is the chief of police, whose man (the governor, الوالي) metes out the punishment.

sentences.t: فَضَرَبَهُ بِالسِّيَاطِ وَرَكَّبَهُ جَمَلًا وَدَوْرَةَ الْمَدِينَةِ وَالنَّاسُ يُنَادُونَ عَلَيْهِ هَذَا جَزَاءُ مَنْ يَهْجُمُ عَلَى حَرِيمِ النَّاسِ وَنُفِيَ مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍarabahu bi-al-siyāṭi wa-rakkabahu jamalan wa-dawrata al-madīnati wa-al-nāsu yunādūna ʿalayhi hādhā jazāʾu man yahjumu ʿalā ḥarīmi al-nāsi wa-nufiya mina al-madīnati
sentences.l: So he struck him with the whips, and mounted him on a camel, and a circuit of the city, while the people were calling upon him: This is the recompense of whoever assaults upon the harem of the people. And he was banished from the city.
sentences.i: The governor had him flogged, mounted him on a camel, and had him paraded round the city while the crowd cried out before him, "This is the reward of the man who breaks in on other people's women!" And he was banished from the city.
sentences.n: The print has ودورة المدينة, with a final ة where one expects ه, i.e. وَدَوَّرَهُ الْمَدِينَةَ, "and took him round the city". The word is pointed as printed, a noun "a circuit" in the accusative, and the sense is the same; it is probably a misprint. حَرِيمُ النَّاسِ is the women's quarters, hence the women, of other men's households: the crime named is entering another man's harem. Public parading on a camel after a flogging is the standard punishment of shame. يُنَادُونَ عَلَيْهِ is "they proclaim over him", a crier's work.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَ لَا يَدْرِي أيْنَ يَقْصِدُ فَخِفْتُ أنَا فَلَحِقْتُهُ وَالْتَزَمْتُ بِهِ وَرَدَّتُهُ وَأجْلَسْتُهُ عِنْدِي إلَى الْآنِ
sentences.tr: fa-kharaja lā yadrī ayna yaqṣidu fa-khiftu anā fa-laḥiqtuhu wa-iltazamtu bihi wa-raddtuhu wa-ajlastuhu ʿindī ilā al-āni
sentences.l: So he went out, not knowing where he should head; and I feared, I, and I overtook him, and I clung to him, and I turned him back, and I made him sit at my place until now.
sentences.i: So he left, not knowing where to turn. I was afraid for him, and I went after him, caught up with him and embraced him, brought him back, and made him sit with me, where he is to this day.
sentences.n: Here the lame young man's narrative (the barber's speech to the caliph) shifts back to the first person. وَرَدَّتُهُ is printed ردته: the verb رَدَّ "to return" is a doubled verb, whose classical first-person form is رَدَدْتُهُ; the print writes the doubled د once and it is pointed so, to be read raddtuhu, "I turned him back". The word الان is printed without any sign of the long alif; the madda (ٓ) shown on its second alif is our pointing for al-ān, "now". إِلَى الْآنِ, "until now", means he is still with the barber.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَ الْخَلِيفَةُ مِنْ كَلَامِي وَقَالَ أحْسَنْتَ يَا صَامِتُ يَا قَلِيلَ الْكَلَامِ وَأمَرَ لِي بِجَائِزَةٍ وَانْصِرَافٍ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥika al-khalīfatu min kalāmī wa-qāla aḥsanta yā ṣāmitu yā qalīla al-kalāmi wa-amara lī bi-jāʾizatin wa-inṣirāfin
sentences.l: So the caliph laughed at my speech and said: You have done well, O Silent, O few-of-speech; and he commanded for me a prize and a dismissal.
sentences.i: The caliph laughed at my words and said, "Well done, Silent One, man of few words!" And he ordered a reward for me, and my dismissal.
sentences.n: The barber is quoting the caliph (al-Mustanṣir), and the irony of يَا قَلِيلَ الْكَلَامِ, "O few of speech", is the joke of the whole episode: the barber has been talking for pages. أَمَرَ لِي بِجَائِزَةٍ is the verb of ordering that takes لِـ for the person who is to receive the gift. الصامت is vocative with a bare nominative, يَا صَامِتُ, as is regular for a name addressed.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَا أقْبَلُ شَيْأً مِنْكَ دُونَ أنْ أحْكِيَ لَكَ مَا وَقَعَ لِبَقِيَّةِ إخْوَتِي وَلَا تَحْسِبْ أنِّي كَثِيرُ الْكَلَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lā aqbalu shayʾan minka dūna an aḥkiya laka mā waqaʿa li-baqiyyati ikhwatī wa-lā taḥsib annī kathīru al-kalāmi
sentences.l: So I said: I will not accept a thing from you without that I relate to you what befell the remainder of my brothers; and do not reckon that I am much of speech.
sentences.i: But I said, "I will accept nothing from you until I have told you what happened to the rest of my brothers, and do not think me a man of many words."
sentences.n: The barber, undaunted, refuses the reward until he has told the caliph the stories of his other brothers. دُونَ أَنْ is here "before, short of" and means "unless first". The print spells شيأ with the hamza on a separate alif, which is why the final alif of the tanwīn is pointed شَيْأً.

sentences.t: اِعْلَمْ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنَّ أَخِي الثَّانِيَ كَانَ اسْمُهُ بَقْبَاتَهْ وَهُوَ الْمَفْلُوجُ
sentences.tr: iʿlam yā amīra al-muʾminīna anna akhī al-thāniya kāna ismuhu baqbātah wa-huwa al-maflūju
sentences.l: Know, O commander of the believers, that my brother the second, his-name was Baqbāta, and he (was) the paralysed-one.
sentences.i: Know, O Commander of the Faithful, that my second brother was named Baqbāta, and he was the paralysed one.
sentences.n: The name بقباته is obscure; it may be a variant of the baqbūq of the opening list, but that list gave the second brother as al-Haddār, so the print's naming of the brothers is not consistent from page to page. I read it Baqbātah with a final sukūn, as a proper name. المفلوج is "struck with paralysis" (from falaja), not merely lame.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ وَقَعَ لَهُ فِي بَعْضِ الْأَيَّامِ أَنَّهُ كَانَ مَاشِيًا أِلَى حَاجَةٍ لَهُ وَإِذَا هُوَ بِعَجُوزٍ قَدِ اسْتَقْبَلَتْهُ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qad waqaʿa lahu fī baʿḍi al-ayyāmi annahu kāna māshiyan ilā ḥājatin lahu wa-idhā huwa bi-ʿajūzin qadi istaqbalat-hu wa-qālat lahu
sentences.l: And indeed it befell to-him in some of the days that he was walking to a need of his, and behold, he (was) with an old woman, who had met him, and she said to him:
sentences.i: And it happened to him one day that he was walking to see about some errand of his, when suddenly an old woman came to meet him and said to him,
sentences.n: وَإِذَا هُوَ بِعَجُوزٍ: after إِذَا of surprise the بِـ only marks what appears ("and behold, an old woman"). The verb that follows, قَدِ اسْتَقْبَلَتْهُ, describes her.

sentences.t: أَيُّهَا الرَّجُلُ قِفْ قَلِيلًا حَتَّى أَعْرِضَ عَلَيْكَ أَمْرًا فَأِنْ أَعْجَبَكَ فَاقْضِهِ لِي وَاسْتَخِرِاللَّهَ
sentences.tr: ayyuhā al-rajulu qif qalīlan ḥattā aʿriḍa ʿalayka amran fa-in aʿjabaka fa-uqḍihi lī wa-istakhiri Allāha
sentences.l: O you man, stop a little until I present to-you a matter; and if it pleases you, then accomplish it for me, and ask-God's-choice.
sentences.i: "Sir, stop a moment while I put a matter before you; and if it pleases you, then carry it out for me, and ask God to guide your choice."
sentences.n: واستخرالله is printed as one word, with no space before the divine name: istakhir Allāh, "seek God's best choice" (the root of the prayer istikhāra). The final كَسْرة on the verb is the linking vowel before the alif of the article.

sentences.t: فَوَقَفَ أَخِي فَقَالَتْ أَقُولُ لَكَ عَلَى شَيٌ وَأُرْشِدُكَ أِلَيْهِ وَلَا يَكُونُ كَلَامُكَ كَثِيرًا
sentences.tr: fa-waqafa akhī fa-qālat aqūlu laka ʿalā shayʾun wa-urshiduka ilayhi wa-lā yakūnu kalāmuka kathīran
sentences.l: So my brother stopped, and she said: I will tell you of a thing and guide you to it, and your speech must not be much.
sentences.i: So my brother stopped, and she said, "I shall tell you of something and guide you to it; only do not let your talk run long."
sentences.n: The print puts a damma-tanwīn on شيٌ, which I keep and read shayʾun; after عَلَى a genitive شَيْءٍ would be expected, so the mark is either a slip or the print treating the phrase as quoted. وَلَا يَكُونُ كَلَامُكَ is an injunction in the indicative ("and your talk is not to be much"); it sets up the old woman's later reproach, "did I not tell you not to talk much?".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا أَخِي هَاتِي كَلَامَكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā akhī hātī kalāmaki
sentences.l: So he said to her, my brother: Bring your speech.
sentences.i: My brother said to her, "Out with it, then."
sentences.n: هَاتِ is the colloquial-flavoured imperative "bring"; here with the feminine -ī because he addresses the woman. "Bring your speech" is a plain way of saying "say what you have to say".

sentences.t: قَالَتْ لَهُ مَا قَوْلُكَ فِي دَارٍ حَسَنَةٍ وَرَوْضَةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ مَاؤُهَا يَجْرِي وَفَاكِهَةٍ وَمُدَامٍ وَوَجْهٍ مَلِيحٍ تُعَانِقُهُ مِنَ الْعِشَاءِ أِلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: qālat lahu mā qawluka fī dārin ḥasanatin wa-rawḍatin ṭayyibatin māʾuhā yajrī wa-fākihatin wa-mudāmin wa-wajhin malīḥin tuʿāniquhu mina al-ʿishāʾi ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: She said to him: What (is) your saying about a house beautiful, and a garden good, its water flowing, and fruit, and wine, and a face handsome you embrace from the evening to the morning?
sentences.i: She said, "What would you say to a lovely house and a pleasant garden with running water, with fruit and wine, and a fair face to hold in your arms from evening to morning?"
sentences.n: مَا قَوْلُكَ فِي … is the stock offer, "what do you say to …?". The last clause, a handsome face you embrace all night, is the old woman's bait, and the story will not bowdlerize what it leads to. مُدَام is wine ("that which is made to last"); Lane has it as old wine kept long in its skin.

sentences.t: فَأِنْ فَعَلْتَ مَا أُشِيرُ لَكَ عَلَيْهِ رَأَيْتَ الْخَيْرَ
sentences.tr: fa-in faʿalta mā ushīru laka ʿalayhi raʾayta al-khayra
sentences.l: And if you do what I point out to you concerning it, you will see the good.
sentences.i: "If you do as I advise you, you will see good come of it."
sentences.n: رَأَيْتَ is a past form standing for the future result of a condition ("you will have seen"), as often in conditional sentences. أَشَارَ عَلَى means to advise someone.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ أَخِي كَلَامَهَا قَالَ لَهَا يَاسِتِّي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa akhī kalāmahā qāla lahā yā sittī
sentences.l: And when my brother heard her speech, he said to her: O my lady,
sentences.i: When my brother heard her words, he said to her, "My lady,
sentences.n: ياستي is printed as one word: yā + sittī, from sitt, "lady" (a contraction of sayyida, very common in Middle Arabic).

sentences.t: وَكَيْفَ قَصَدْتِنِي بِهَذَا الْأَمْرِ دُونَ الْخَلْقِ أَجْمَعِينَ فَأَيْشْ الَّذِي أَعْجَبَكِ مِنِّي
sentences.tr: wa-kayfa qaṣadtinī bi-hādhā al-amri dūna al-khalqi ajmaʿīna fa-aysh alladhī aʿjabaki minnī
sentences.l: and how did you aim at me with this matter, apart-from the creatures altogether, and what (is) that which pleased you of me?
sentences.i: how is it that you chose me for this business out of all the people, and what is it about me that pleased you?"
sentences.n: قَصَدْتِنِي بِـ: qaṣada bi- means to make for or choose someone for a thing; here the speaker is the object. دُونَ here is "to the exclusion of". فَأَيْشْ is the colloquial "what" (a contraction of أَيُّ شَيْءٍ), and الَّذِي follows it as a plain relative: "what is the thing that pleased you".

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لِأَخِي مَا قُلْتُ لَكَ لَاتَكُنْ كَثِيرَ الْكَلَامِ وَاسْكُتْ وَامْضِ مَعِي
sentences.tr: fa-qālat li-akhī mā qultu laka lā-takun kathīra al-kalāmi wa-uskut wa-imḍi maʿī
sentences.l: So she said to my brother: Did I not say to you, "Do not be much-of-speech"? And be silent, and go with me.
sentences.i: She said to my brother, "Did I not tell you not to talk so much? Be quiet and come along with me."
sentences.n: مَا قُلْتُ لَكَ is "did I not tell you?" with a bare مَا as the negative question; Classical would add the hamza of question or use أَلَمْ. لاتكن is printed as one word, lā-takun, "do not be". The imperatives واسكت and وامض are pointed with their alifs of connection, which carry no mark.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ وَلَّتِ الْعَجُوزُ وَأَخِي تَابِعُهَا طَمَعًا فِيمَا وَصَفَتْ لَهُ حَتَّى دَخَلُوا دَارًا فَسِيحَةً كَثِيرَةَ الْخَدَمِ
sentences.tr: thumma wallati al-ʿajūzu wa-akhī tābiʿuhā ṭamaʿan fīmā waṣafat lahu ḥattā dakhalū dāran fasīḥatan kathīrata al-khadami
sentences.l: Then the old woman turned away, and my brother (was) following her, in greed for what she had described to him, until they entered a house spacious, many-of-servants.
sentences.i: Then the old woman turned and went, and my brother followed after her, greedy for what she had described to him, until they entered a spacious house with many servants.
sentences.n: دَخَلُوا is a masculine plural for the two of them, which is common in the Nights. وَاخِى تَابِعُهَا is a circumstantial clause with the participle, "while my brother (was) her follower".

sentences.t: وَصَعِدَتْ بِهِ مِنْ أَدْنَى أِلَى أَعْلَا فَرَأَى قَصْرًا ظَرِيفًا
sentences.tr: wa-ṣaʿidat bihi min adnā ilā aʿlā fa-raʾā qaṣran ẓarīfan
sentences.l: And she went up with him from lowest to highest, and he saw a palace elegant.
sentences.i: She took him up from the lowest part to the highest, and he saw a handsome palace.
sentences.n: وَصَعِدَتْ بِهِ: the بِـ makes the intransitive verb "go up" take someone along, "she took him up". مِنْ أَدْنَى إِلَى أَعْلَا is "from the lowest to the highest". The print writes أَعْلَى with a final alif (اعلا).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهُ أَهْلُ الْبَيْتِ قَالُوا لَهُ مَنِ الَّذِي أَوْصَلَكَ أِلَى هُنَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhu ahlu al-bayti qālū lahu mani alladhī awṣalaka ilā hunā
sentences.l: And when the people of the house saw him, they said to him: Who (is) the one who brought you to here?
sentences.i: When the people of the house saw him, they said to him, "Who brought you here?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُمُ الْعَجُوزُ اُسْكُتُوا عَنْهُ وَلَا تُكَدِّرُوا قَلْبَهُ فَأِنَّهُ صَانِعٌ وَنَحْنُ مُحْتَاجُونَ أِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahumu al-ʿajūzu uskutū ʿanhu wa-lā tukaddirū qalbahu fa-innahu ṣāniʿun wa-naḥnu muḥtājūna ilayhi
sentences.l: So the old woman said to them: Be silent concerning him, and do not muddy his heart, for he (is) a craftsman and we (are) in-need of him.
sentences.i: The old woman said to them, "Leave him be, and do not trouble his mind, for he is a craftsman and we have need of him."
sentences.n: Note the verb: اُسْكُتُوا عَنْهُ is "be silent about him", that is, do not question him. كَدَّرَ is to make turbid, to cloud (of water); "do not cloud his heart" means do not upset him. The "craftsman" is the cover story that gets him through the door.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَنَّهَا مَشَتْ بِهِ أِلَى غُرْفَةٍ مُزَيَّنَةٍ لَمْ تَرَ الْعُيُونُ أَحْسَنَ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: thumma annahā mashat bihi ilā ghurfatin muzayyanatin lam tara al-ʿuyūnu aḥsana minhā
sentences.l: Then, that she walked with him to a room adorned, the eyes had not seen better than it.
sentences.i: Then she led him to a decorated room, finer than any eyes had seen.
sentences.n: ثُمَّ أَنَّهَا is a narrator's "and then, she …" with أَنَّ used as a pure connective. مَشَتْ بِهِ, with the بِـ of accompaniment, "she walked with him", that is, led him. لَمْ تَرَ الْعُيُونُ أَحْسَنَ مِنْهَا is the stock hyperbole for a room without equal.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا الْغُرْفَةَ قَامَتِ النِّسْوَانُ وَرَحَّبْنَ بِهِ وَأَجْلَسْنَهُ بِجَنْبِهِمْ فَلَمْ يَلْبَثْ أِذْ سَمِعَ جَلَبَةً عَظِيمَةً
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhalū al-ghurfata qāmati al-niswānu wa-raḥḥabna bihi wa-ajlasnahu bi-janbihim fa-lam yalbath idh samiʿa jalabatan ʿaẓīmatan
sentences.l: And when they entered the room, the women stood, and they welcomed him, and they seated him at their side, and he had not lingered when he heard a clamour great.
sentences.i: When they entered the room the women rose and welcomed him and seated him beside them; and he had not been there long when he heard a great commotion,
sentences.n: بِجَنْبِهِمْ has the masculine -hum for a group of women, as also in the next clause; Middle Arabic often drops the feminine plural pronoun. فَلَمْ يَلْبَثْ إِذْ … is "he had not lingered when …", the idiom for "hardly had he stayed when". رَحَّبَ بِـ is "to bid welcome", from the root of raḥb, "roomy".

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِجَوَارٍ قَدْ أَقْبَلْنَ وَفِي وَسْطِهِنَّ جَارِيَةٌ كَالْبَدْرِ فِي لَيْلَةِ تَمَامِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-jawārin qad aqbalna wa-fī wasaṭihinna jāriyatun ka-al-badri fī laylati tamāmihi
sentences.l: and behold, with girls who had come forward, and in the midst of them a girl like the full moon in the night of its completeness.
sentences.i: and suddenly a troop of girls came in, and in their midst a girl like the moon on the night of its fullness.
sentences.n: كَالْبَدْرِ: the كَـ prefix is "like". لَيْلَةُ تَمَامِهِ, "the night of its completeness", is the fourteenth night of the lunar month, when the moon is full.

sentences.t: فَمَدَّ أَخِي نَظَرَهُ أِلَيْهَا وَقَامَ قَائِمًا وَخَدَمَهَا فَرَحَّبَتْ بِهِ وَأَمَرَتْهُ بِالْجُلُوسِ فَجَلَسَ
sentences.tr: fa-madda akhī naẓarahu ilayhā wa-qāma qāʾiman wa-khadamahā fa-raḥḥabat bihi wa-amarat-hu bi-al-julūsi fa-jalasa
sentences.l: So my brother stretched his gaze to her, and stood up standing, and served her; so she welcomed him and ordered him to the sitting, and he sat.
sentences.i: My brother fixed his eyes on her, and rose to his feet and paid her homage; she welcomed him and bade him sit, and he sat.
sentences.n: قَامَ قَائِمًا is "he stood up standing", the emphatic cognate-participle. خَدَمَهَا, "he served her", here means he paid her homage, with a bow or salutation. أَمَرَهُ بِـ is "to command someone to do" (أَمَرَ takes بِـ for the thing ordered).

sentences.t: فَأَقْبَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ أَعَزَّكَ اللَّهُ هَلْ فِيكَ خَيْرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-aqbalat ʿalayhi wa-qālat lahu aʿazzaka Allāhu hal fīka khayrun
sentences.l: Then she turned toward him and said to him: God honour you! Is there in you good?
sentences.i: She turned to him and said, "God honour you! Is there any good in you?"
sentences.n: هَلْ فِيكَ خَيْرٌ is the question "are you any good?", and in the Nights it is a question about his readiness for pleasure. His answer in the next sentence, that all good is in him, is the expected one.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَخِي يَا سَيِّدَتِي الْخَيْرُ كُلُّهُ فِيَّ ثُمَّ أَمَرَتْ بِإِحْضَارِ الطَّعَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla akhī yā sayyidatī al-khayru kulluhu fīya thumma amarat bi-iḥḍāri al-ṭaʿāmi
sentences.l: So my brother said: O my mistress, the good, all of it, (is) in me. Then she ordered the bringing-present of the food,
sentences.i: My brother said, "My lady, all good is in me." Then she ordered the food to be brought,
sentences.n: The print puts a shadda on the yā' of فيّ, which I keep (fīya, "in me"). أَمَرَتْ بِإِحْضَارِ: the verb of command takes بِـ before the thing ordered.

sentences.t: فَقَدَّمُوا لَهَا طَعَامًا حَسَنًا فَجَلَسَتْ تَأْكُلُ وَالْجَارِيَةُ مَعَ ذٰلِكَ لَاتَهْتَدِي مِنَ الضَّحِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qaddamū lahā ṭaʿāman ḥasanan fa-jalasat taʾkulu wa-al-jāriyatu maʿa dhālika lā-tahtadī mina al-ḍaḥiki
sentences.l: So they set before her food beautiful, and she sat eating, while the girl, with that, was not guided from the laughter.
sentences.i: They set fine food before her, and she sat down to eat, while the girl all the while could not stop laughing.
sentences.n: تَا^ْكُلُ is printed تاكل with a bare alif; it is taʾkul ("eats"). لَاتَهْتَدِي مِنَ الضَّحِكِ, "is not guided from laughing", is an idiom for being unable to check one's laughter. The noun lā-tahtadī is printed as one word.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا نَظَرَ أِلَيْهَا أَخِي تَغِيبُ إِىٰ جَوَارِهَا كَأَنَّهَا تَضْحَكُ مِنْهُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā naẓara ilayhā akhī taghību ilā jawārihā ka-annahā taḍḥaku minhum
sentences.l: And whenever my brother looked at her, she would withdraw to her girls, as if laughing at them.
sentences.i: Whenever my brother looked at her she would slip away among her girls, as though she were laughing at them.
sentences.n: اى is printed where إِلَى is needed; I read it as إِلَى with the lām dropped (the alternative, أَيْ "that is", gives no good sense). جوارها: the final yā' of the defective plural is not written (expected جَوَارِيهَا); I read jawārihā as printed. وَإِذَا here is "whenever", not the "behold" of surprise. مِنْهُمْ is again a masculine pronoun for women.

sentences.t: وَتُظْهِرُ لِأَخِي الْمَوَدَّةَ وَتَمْزَحُ مَعَهُ وَأَخِى الْحِمَارُ لَا يَفْهَمُ شَيْأً
sentences.tr: wa-tuẓhiru li-akhī al-mawaddata wa-tamzaḥu maʿahu wa-akhī al-ḥimāru lā yafhamu shayʾan
sentences.l: And she showed to my brother affection, and joked with him, and my brother the ass understands nothing.
sentences.i: and she showed my brother affection and teased him, while my brother, the ass, understood nothing.
sentences.n: الحمار, "the ass", is the narrator's own verdict on his brother (he is the barber, telling a story in which he mocks the family). The print spells واخى with a dotless final yā' (ى); I read it akhī as everywhere else. The li- of لِأَخِي marks the person to whom the affection is shown.

sentences.t: وَمِنْ كَثْرَةِ مَا غَلَبَ عَلَيْهِ الشَّوْقُ يَعْتَقِدُأَنَّ الْجَارِيَةَ عَاشِقَةٌ عَلَيْهِ وَأَنَّهَا تُبَلِّغُهُ أِلَى مُنَاهُ
sentences.tr: wa-min kathrati mā ghalaba ʿalayhi al-shawqu yaʿtaqidu anna al-jāriyata ʿāshiqatun ʿalayhi wa-annahā tuballighuhu ilā munāhu
sentences.l: And from the abundance of what longing overcame him, he believes that the girl (is) in-love upon him, and that she will bring him to his wish.
sentences.i: And so overcome was he by longing that he believed the girl was in love with him and would bring him to his desire.
sentences.n: يَعْتَقِدُا^َنَّ is printed as one word (yaʿtaqidu anna), with no space before أَنَّ. مِنْ كَثْرَةِ مَا … is "from the abundance of what …", a causal phrase, "so greatly had longing overcome him". The verb is in the present ("he believes") though the narrative is in the past, as the Nights often does. عَاشِقَةٌ عَلَيْهِ with عَلَى is colloquial for "in love with him" (Classical would use فِي or no preposition).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغُوا مِنَ الطَّعَامِ قَدَّمُوا الْمُدَامَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghū mina al-ṭaʿāmi qaddamū al-mudāma
sentences.l: And when they had finished with the food, they set out the wine.
sentences.i: When they had finished eating they brought out the wine,

sentences.t: ثُمَّ حَضَرْنَ عَشْرُ جَوَارٍ كَأَنَّهُنَّ أَقْمَارٌ وَبِأَيْدِيهِنَّ الْعِيدَانُ ذَوَاتُ الْأَوْتَارِ
sentences.tr: thumma ḥaḍarna ʿashru jawārin ka-annahunna aqmārun wa-bi-aydīhinna al-ʿīdānu dhawātu al-awtāri
sentences.l: Then there came ten girls, as if they (were) moons, and in their hands the lutes, the having-ones of the strings,
sentences.i: and then ten girls came in, like moons, with lutes in their hands, strung and ready,
sentences.n: حَضَرْنَ عَشْرُ جَوَارٍ has the verb in the feminine plural before its plural subject, which Classical grammar would not allow (it would put the verb singular). ذَوَاتُ الْأَوْتَارِ, "possessors of strings", is a common way to say stringed.

sentences.t: فَجَعَلْنَ يُغَنِّينَ بِكُلِّ صَوْتٍ شَجِيٍّ
sentences.tr: fa-jaʿalna yughanninā bi-kulli ṣawtin shajiyyin
sentences.l: And they began to sing with every voice-tune moving.
sentences.i: and they began to sing, each in a plaintive, moving air.
sentences.n: غَنَّى بِـ is to sing something, here a tune; صَوْت is the musical term for a song or air, not just a voice. شَجِيّ is "melancholy, touching".

sentences.t: فَغَلَبَ الطَّرَبُ عَلَى أَخِي وَتَنَاوَلَ قَدَحًا مِنْ يَدِهَا فَشَرِبَهُ فَقَامَ لَهَا قَائِمًا
sentences.tr: fa-ghalaba al-ṭarabu ʿalā akhī wa-tanāwala qadaḥan min yadihā fa-sharibahu fa-qāma lahā qāʾiman
sentences.l: So delight overcame my brother, and he took a cup from her hand and drank it, and stood up for her, standing.
sentences.i: Rapture overcame my brother; he took a cup from her hand and drank it, and rose to his feet before her.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَنَّ الصَّبِيَّةَ شَرِبَتْ قَدَحًا فَقَالَ لَهَا أَخِي صِحَّةً وَخَدَمَهَا
sentences.tr: thumma anna al-ṣabiyyata sharibat qadaḥan fa-qāla lahā akhī ṣiḥḥatan wa-khadamahā
sentences.l: Then that the young girl drank a cup, and my brother said to her: Health! and served her.
sentences.i: Then the girl drank a cup, and my brother said to her, "Your health!" and paid her homage.
sentences.n: صِحَّةً, "health", is the toast, in the accusative as an elliptical wish ("[I wish] health"). خَدَمَهَا is again "he paid her homage".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَسْقَتْهُ قَدَحًا فَشَرِبَ وَصَفَعَتْهُ عَلَى رَقَبَتِهِ فَكُلَّمَا رَأَى أَخِي ذٰلِكَ مِنْهَا خَرَجَ فِي أَشَدِّ خُرُوجٍ
sentences.tr: thumma asqat-hu qadaḥan fa-shariba wa-ṣafaʿat-hu ʿalā raqabatihi fa-kullamā raʾā akhī dhālika minhā kharaja fī ashaddi khurūjin
sentences.l: Then she gave him a cup to drink, and he drank, and she slapped him on his neck; and each time my brother saw that from her, he went out in the severest of exits.
sentences.i: Then she gave him a cup to drink, and he drank, and she struck him on the neck; and each time my brother saw such a thing from her he burst out of the room in a fury.
sentences.n: صَفَعَ is to slap, especially on the back of the neck, and the humiliating slap is what the whole episode turns on; the girls' jokes are cruel, and the narrator does not soften them. فِي أَشَدِّ خُرُوجٍ is a superlative of manner: "in the hardest of exits", that is, in the most violent haste.

sentences.t: فَتَبِعَتْهُ الْعَجُوزُ وَجَعَلَتْ تَغْمِزُهُ بِعَيْنِهَا يَعْنِي ارْجِعْ فَرَجَعَ
sentences.tr: fa-tabiʿat-hu al-ʿajūzu wa-jaʿalat taghmizuhu bi-ʿaynihā yaʿnī irjiʿ fa-rajaʿa
sentences.l: So the old woman followed him, and began to wink at him with her eye, meaning: Go back! And he went back.
sentences.i: The old woman followed him and began winking at him, as if to say, "Come back," and he went back.
sentences.n: يَعْنِي ارْجِعْ is the narrator's gloss on the wink, "meaning: come back". غَمَزَ بِعَيْنِهِ is the regular expression for "wink", with بِـ of instrument.

sentences.t: فَأَمَرَتْهُ الْجَارِيَةُ بِالْجُلُوسِ فَجَلَسَ وَجَلَسَ وَلَمْ يَنْطِقْ فَعَادَتِ الصَّفْعُ عَلَى قَفَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-amarat-hu al-jāriyatu bi-al-julūsi fa-jalasa wa-jalasa wa-lam yanṭiq fa-ʿādati al-ṣafʿu ʿalā qafāhu
sentences.l: So the girl ordered him to sit, and he sat, and sat, and did not speak, and the slapping returned on the nape of his neck.
sentences.i: The girl ordered him to sit; he sat, and went on sitting, and said not a word, and the slaps came raining on the back of his neck again.
sentences.n: The doubled فَجَلَسَ وَجَلَسَ is printed so; it reads "he sat, and sat" (kept as printed), of a man who stays put and keeps quiet as he was told. عَادَتِ الصَّفْعُ pairs a feminine verb with the masculine verbal noun, a lapse of agreement. قَفَاهُ is the nape.

sentences.t: وَمَا كَفَاهَا ذٰلِكَ حَتَّى أَمَرَتْ جَوَارِهَا كُلَّهَا أَنْ يَصْفَعُوهُ
sentences.tr: wa-mā kafāhā dhālika ḥattā amarat jawārihā kullahā an yaṣfaʿūhu
sentences.l: And that did not suffice her until she ordered her girls, all of them, that they slap him,
sentences.i: Nor was that enough for her: she ordered all her girls to slap him,
sentences.n: جوارها: as above, the defective plural lacks its written yā' (expected جَوَارِيَهَا); I read it as printed. أَمَرَتْ … أَنْ يَصْفَعُوهُ is the regular "she ordered that they …", with the subjunctive and the masculine plural for girls.

sentences.t: وَهُوَ يَقُولُ لِلْعَجُوزِ مَا رَأَيْتُ شَيْأً أَحْسَنَ مِنْ هَذَا
sentences.tr: wa-huwa yaqūlu li-al-ʿajūzi mā raʾaytu shayʾan aḥsana min hādhā
sentences.l: while he was saying to the old woman: I have not seen anything better than this.
sentences.i: while he said to the old woman, "I have never seen anything finer than this!"
sentences.n: Here is the foolish man's reaction, which the narrator will not excuse: he calls the beating the finest thing he has seen. مَا رَأَيْتُ is "I have not seen" (the past with مَا).

sentences.t: فَتَقُولُ الْعَجُوزُ أَيْ وَحَقِّكِ يَا مَوْلَاتِي
sentences.tr: fa-taqūlu al-ʿajūzu ay wa-ḥaqqiki yā mawlātī
sentences.l: And the old woman says: Yes, by your right, O my mistress,
sentences.i: and the old woman answers, "Yes, by your life, my lady,
sentences.n: أَيْ وَحَقِّكِ is "yes, by your right", an oath of agreement (أَيْ is "yes", not the explanatory "that is"); the old woman turns to the girl and speaks, as if the brother's remark had been addressed to her. The unit ends here because the printed line does; the speech continues in the next slice. The tense (فَتَقُولُ, present) is again historic present.

sentences.t: فَصَفَعَتْهُ الْجَوَارِإِلَى أَنْ أُغْمِيَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣafaʿathu al-jawāri ilā an ughmiya ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And they-slapped him, the maids, until it-was-covered-over upon him.
sentences.i: And the maids slapped him until he fell senseless.
sentences.n: The print runs الجوار and الى together and leaves out the yā' of الجواري; the kasra on the rā' stands for that dropped -ī (so throughout: الجوار is read al-jawārī). أُغْمِيَ عَلَيْهِ, "it was covered over upon him", is the idiom for fainting.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَامَ أَخِي لِقَضَاءِ حَاجَتِهِ فَلَحِقَتْهُ الْعَجُوزُ
sentences.tr: thumma qāma akhī li-qaḍāʾi ḥājatihi fa-laḥiqathu al-ʿajūzu
sentences.l: Then my brother rose for the fulfilling of his need, and the old woman caught-up-with him.
sentences.i: Then my brother got up to relieve himself, and the old woman went after him.
sentences.n: قضاء الحاجة, "fulfilling a need", is the ordinary polite phrase for going to the privy.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لَهُ اصْبِرْ قَلِيلًا تَبْلُغْ مَا تُرِيدُ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat lahu iṣbir qalīlan tablugh mā turīdu
sentences.l: Then she said to him: Be-patient a little; you-will-reach what you want.
sentences.i: Then she said to him, "Be patient a little longer and you will have what you want."
sentences.n: The jussive تَبْلُغْ after an imperative is the old conditional: "be patient, you will reach".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَهَاأَخِي إِلَى كَمْ أَصْبِرُ وَقَدْ أُغْمِيَ عَلَيَّ مِنَ الصَّفْعِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ahāakhī ilā kam aṣbiru wa-qad ughmiya ʿalayya mina al-ṣafʿi
sentences.l: So he said: Ahā, my-brother! Until how-much shall I be-patient, when I-was already covered-over upon me from the slapping?
sentences.i: He cried, "Ah, brother! How long must I be patient, when the slaps have already knocked me senseless?"
sentences.n: اهااخي is one printed word. I read it as an interjection أَهَا ("ah!") run into أَخِي ("my brother"), but it is odd for a man to call an old woman "brother", so the form may be corrupt; I cannot name a better candidate. The print has no mark on عليّ; the shadda is ours.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ إِذَا سَكِرَتْ بَلَغْتَ مُرَادَكَ فَرَجَعَ أَخِي إِلَى مَكَانِهِ وَجَلَسَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu idhā sakirat balaghta murādaka fa-rajaʿa akhī ilā makānihi wa-jalasa
sentences.l: So she said to him: When she-gets-drunk, you-reach your-aim. So my brother returned to his place and sat.
sentences.i: She said, "Once she is drunk, you will have your desire." So my brother went back to his place and sat down.
sentences.n: سكرت is unpointed in the print. Since the old woman is talking about the lady, and says later that it is the lady's habit to grow drunk, I read it as third feminine ("she gets drunk"); "you get drunk" (سَكِرْتَ) would be the other possibility. The perfect after إِذَا refers to the future.

sentences.t: فَقَامَتِ الْجَوَارِ عَنْ آخِرِهِمْ فَأَمَرَتْهُمْ أَنْ يُبَخِّرُوهُ وَأَنْ يَرُشُّوا عَلَى وَجْهِهِ الْمَا وَرْدٍ فَفَعَلْنَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāmati al-jawāri ʿan ākhirihim fa-amarahum an yubakhkhirūhu wa-an yarushshū ʿalā wajhihi al-mā wardin fa-faʿalna dhālika
sentences.l: So the maids rose, from their last; and she ordered them that they perfume-him-with-incense and that they sprinkle upon his face the water rose; so they-(f.)-did that.
sentences.i: Then all the maids rose, down to the last of them, and she ordered them to fumigate him with incense and to sprinkle rose-water on his face; and they did so.
sentences.n: عَنْ آخِرِهِمْ, "from their last", means "every one of them". الما ورد is ماء ورد, "rose-water", printed with the hamza missing and as two words; ward stands in the genitive after the first term. Note the shift of gender: the maids are أَمَرَتْهُمْ (masculine) but فَعَلْنَ (feminine). The print keeps the precomposed آ in آخِرِهِمْ.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لَهُ الصَّبِيَّةُ أَعَزَّكَ اللَّهُ قَدْ دَخَلْتَ مَنْزِلِى وَصَبَرْتَ عَلَى شَرْطِي وَأَيُّ مَنْ خَالَفَنِي طَرَدْتُهُ وَمَنْ صَبَرَ بَلَغَ مُرَادَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahu al-ṣabiyyatu aʿazzaka Allāhu qad dakhalta manzilī wa-ṣabarta ʿalā sharṭī wa-ayyu man khālafanī ṭaradtuhu wa-man ṣabara balagha murādahu
sentences.l: And she said to him, the young-woman: God has-made-you-mighty! You have entered my-house and been-patient upon my condition; and which-one who opposed me, I-drove-him-out; and whoever was-patient reached his aim.
sentences.i: And the girl said to him, "God give you honour: you have entered my house and borne with my terms. Whoever has crossed me I have driven out, and whoever is patient gets what he wants."
sentences.n: أَعَزَّكَ اللَّهُ is a courtesy formula, "may God exalt you". وَأَيُّ مَنْ خَالَفَنِي is literally "and which of those who opposed me", i.e. "whoever opposed me"; the pronoun in طَرَدْتُهُ takes it up. The final ى of منزلى is the edition's.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا أَخِي يَا سَيِّدَتِي أَنَا عَبْدُكِ وَفِي طَبَقَةِ يَدِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā akhī yā sayyidatī anā ʿabduki wa-fī ṭabaqati yadiki
sentences.l: So my brother said to her: O my mistress, I am your slave, and in the layer of your hand.
sentences.i: My brother said to her, "My lady, I am your slave, wholly in your hand."
sentences.n: طبقة is "layer, stratum, grade". I cannot cite a fixed phrase "in the layer of your hand"; the sense is plainly "in your power".

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ اعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَشْغَفَنِي بِحُبِّ الطَّرَبِ فَمَنْ أَطَاعَنِي نَالَ مَايُرِيدُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu iʿlam anna Allāha ashghafanī bi-ḥubbi al-ṭarabi fa-man aṭāʿanī nāla māyurīdu
sentences.l: So she said to him: Know that God has made-me-passion-struck with love of the delight-in-song; so whoever obeys me gets what-he-wants.
sentences.i: She said to him, "Know that God has made me mad for music; whoever obeys me gets what he wants."
sentences.n: أَشْغَفَنِي is the fourth form of شَغَفَ ("to be smitten to the heart"), a rare causative: "made me love passionately". الطرب is the stirring of the heart by song. مايريد is printed as one word.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَمَرَتِ الْجَوَارِأَنْ يُغَنِّينَ بِأَصْوَاتٍ عَالِيَةٍ حَتَّى طَرِبَ الْمَجْلِسُ
sentences.tr: thumma amarati al-jawāri an yughanniyna bi-aṣwātin ʿāliyatin ḥattā ṭariba al-majlisu
sentences.l: Then she ordered the maids that they sing with voices high, until the assembly was-stirred-with-song.
sentences.i: Then she ordered the maids to sing in loud voices, until the whole company was swept away with delight.
sentences.n: Again two printed words run together: الجوار and أن.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لِبَعْضِ الْجَوَارِ خُذِي سَيِّدَكِ وَاقْضِي حَاجَتَهُ وَائْتِينِي بِهِ فِي الْحَالِ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat li-baʿḍi al-jawāri khudhī sayyidaki wa-iqḍī ḥājatahu wa-itīnī bihi fī al-ḥāli
sentences.l: Then she said to some-of the maids: Take your-master, and fulfil his need, and bring-me with-him in the instant.
sentences.i: Then she said to one of the maids, "Take your master, see to his need, and bring him back to me at once."
sentences.n: The same phrase قضاء الحاجة as above, but here it is the pretext for what follows: the dyeing and shaving. سَيِّدَكِ, "your master", is said to a woman, hence the -ki.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ أَخِى وَهُوَ لَايَدْرِي مَا تَصْنَعُ بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhati al-jāriyatu akhī wa-huwa lāyadrī mā taṣnaʿu bihi
sentences.l: So the girl took my brother, and he not-knowing what she would-do with him.
sentences.i: So the maid led my brother away, though he had no idea what she meant to do with him.
sentences.n: لايدري is printed as one word. The ى of أخى is the edition's.

sentences.t: فَلَحِقَتْهُ الْعَجُوزُ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ اصْبِرْ مَا بَقِيَ إِلَّا الْقَلِيلُ فَرَاقَ وَجْهُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-laḥiqathu al-ʿajūzu wa-qālat lahu iṣbir mā baqiya illā al-qalīlu farāqa wajhuhu
sentences.l: So the old woman caught-up-with him and said to him: Be-patient; nothing remains but the little. And his face cleared.
sentences.i: The old woman caught up with him and said, "Be patient; only a little remains." And his face brightened.
sentences.n: فراق وجهه is not certain. I take it as راق, "to be clear, pleasing", with وجهه as subject: his face cleared. The words might instead belong to the old woman's speech, as "for the beautifying of his face" (the little that remains is the work on his face), but that needs a different vowelling.

sentences.t: فَأَقْبَلَ أَخِي عَلَى الصَّبِيَّةِ وَالْعَجُوزُ تَقُولُ اصْبِرْ فَقَدْ بَلَغْتَ مَاتُرِيدُ
sentences.tr: fa-aqbala akhī ʿalā al-ṣabiyyati wa-al-ʿajūzu taqūlu iṣbir fa-qad balaghta māturīdu
sentences.l: So my brother turned-toward the young-woman, while the old woman (was) saying: Be-patient, for you have reached what-you-want.
sentences.i: My brother came before the girl while the old woman kept saying, "Be patient: you have reached what you want."
sentences.n: وَالْعَجُوزُ تَقُولُ is a circumstantial clause ("with the old woman saying"). ماتريد is printed as one word.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا أَعْلِمِينِي مَا ذَا تُرِيدُ تَعْمَلُ هَذِهِ الْجَارِيَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā aʿlimīnī mā dhā turīdu taʿmalu hādhihi al-jāriyatu
sentences.l: So he said to her: Inform-me, what (is) this, she-wants she-does, this girl?
sentences.i: Then he said to her, "Tell me what this girl wants to do."
sentences.n: تُرِيدُ تَعْمَلُ, "she wants she does", puts two imperfects side by side without أَنْ. This is a standing habit of Middle Arabic and recurs below (تريد تصبغ, أرادت تفعل). We read each verb as printed and move on.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْعَجُوزُ مَا تَمَّ إِلَّا خَيْرًا فَدَيْتُكَ تُرِيدُ تَصْبُغُ حَوَاجِبَكَ وَتَقُصُّ سِبَالَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-ʿajūzu mā tamma illā khayran fadaytuka turīdu taṣbughu ḥawājibaka wa-taquṣṣu sibālaka
sentences.l: So the old woman said: Nothing has-come-about but good, I-ransomed-you! She-wants she-dyes your eyebrows and she-clips your moustaches.
sentences.i: The old woman said, "Nothing but good will come of it, I would give my life for you! She wants to dye your eyebrows and trim your moustache."
sentences.n: فَدَيْتُكَ, "I have ransomed you", is a caressing oath: "may I be your ransom". سبال is the hair of the moustache. The shadda on تمّ is the edition's.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَخِي أَمَّا صَبْغُ الْحَوَاجِبِ فَيَزُولُ بِالْغَسْلِ وَأَمَّا نَتْفُ السِّبَالِ فَهُوَ مِمَّا يُؤْلِمُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla akhī ammā ṣabghu al-ḥawājibi fa-yazūlu bi-al-ghasli wa-ammā natfu al-sibāli fa-huwa mimmā yuʾlimu
sentences.l: So my brother said: As for the dyeing of the eyebrows, it goes-away with the washing; and as for the plucking of the moustaches, it is of that which pains.
sentences.i: My brother said, "The dyeing of the eyebrows will wash off, but the plucking of the moustache is painful."
sentences.n: The edition puts a damma on the first letter of يولم but prints no hamza; we supply it, reading yuʾlimu (fourth form of ألم, "to hurt").

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْعَجُوزُ احْذَرْ تُخَالِفَهَا فَهِيَ قَدْ تَعَلَّقَ قَلْبُهَا بِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-ʿajūzu iḥdhar tukhālifahā fa-hiya qad taʿallaqa qalbuhā bika
sentences.l: So the old woman said: Beware you oppose her; for she, her heart has become-attached to you.
sentences.i: The old woman said, "Take care not to cross her, for her heart has become attached to you."
sentences.n: احذر تخالفها has no أَنْ; we read the second verb as subjunctive, "beware lest you cross her". فَهِيَ قَدْ تَعَلَّقَ قَلْبُهَا puts a pronoun in front of a whole clause ("she — her heart is attached"), as the spoken language does.

sentences.t: فَصَبَرَ أَخِي حَتَّى صُبِغَتْ حَوَاجِبُهُ وَنُتِفَتْ سِبَالُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣabara akhī ḥattā ṣubighat ḥawājibuhu wa-nutifat sibāluhu
sentences.l: So my brother was-patient until his eyebrows were dyed and his moustaches were plucked.
sentences.i: So my brother bore it until his eyebrows were dyed and his moustache plucked.

sentences.t: وَمَضَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ إِى سَيِّدَتِهَا وَأَخْبَرَتْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-maḍati al-jāriyatu ilā sayyidatihā wa-akhbarathā
sentences.l: And the girl went to her mistress and informed her.
sentences.i: Then the maid went to her mistress and reported to her.
sentences.n: The print has اى for الى; the lām is missing. We point what is printed and read ilā.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهَا بَقِيَ شَيْءٌ آخَرُ وَهُوَ أَنْ تَحْلِقِي ذَقْنَهُ حَتَّى يَصِيرَ أَمْرَدًا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahā baqiya shayʾun ākharu wa-huwa an taḥliqī dhaqnahu ḥattā yaṣīra amradan
sentences.l: So she said to her: There remains a thing other, and it is that you shave his chin until he becomes beardless.
sentences.i: She said to her, "One thing more remains: you must shave off his beard, until he is smooth-faced as a boy."
sentences.n: تحلقي is the feminine subjunctive after أَنْ (the final nūn dropped). أمرد is a beardless youth. The edition prints شيءٌ with its hamza and tanwīn and the precomposed آ of آخر; both kept.

sentences.t: فَجَاءَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ وَأَخْبَرَتْهُ بِمَا أَمَرَتْ سَيِّدَتُهَا بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-jāʾati al-jāriyatu wa-akhbaratahu bi-mā amarat sayyidatuhā bihi
sentences.l: So the girl came and informed him of what her-mistress ordered of it.
sentences.i: So the maid came and told him what her mistress had ordered.
sentences.n: أمر takes its object with بِـ: أَمَرَ بِكَذَا, "to order a thing"; بِمَا ... بِهِ is that construction with the relative.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا أَخِي الْأَحْمَقُ وَكَيْفَ أَعْمَلُ فِى فَضِيحَتِي مِنَ النَّاسِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā akhī al-aḥmaqu wa-kayfa aʿmalu fī faḍīḥatī mina al-nāsi
sentences.l: So my brother, the fool, said to her: And how shall I act in my disgrace before the people?
sentences.i: My brother the fool said to her, "And what am I to do about my shame before everyone?"
sentences.n: الأحمق, "the fool", is the narrator's aside on his brother, in apposition to أخي.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ الْعَجُوزُ إِنَّهَا مَا أَرَادَتْ تَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ مَعَكَ إِلَّا لِتَبْقَى أَمْرَدًا بِلَا ذَقَنٍ وَلَا يَبْقَى فِي وَجْهِكَ شَيْءٌ يَشُكُّهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu al-ʿajūzu innahā mā arādat tafʿalu dhālika maʿaka illā li-tabqā amradan bi-lā dhaqanin wa-lā yabqā fī wajhika shayʾun yashukkuhā
