sentences.l: So the old woman said to him: Indeed-she did not want she-does that with you except so-that you-remain beardless, without a chin-beard, and there remain not in your face a thing that pricks her.
sentences.i: The old woman said to him, "She does this to you only so that you may stay smooth-faced, with no beard, and nothing be left on your face to prick her."
sentences.n: يشكها: I take شَكَّ in its sense "to pierce, prick", the stubble pricking her; the other reading, "make her doubt", suits the context less. ما أرادت تفعل again joins two verbs without أَنْ.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهَا صَارَ لَهَا فِي قَلْبِهَا مِنْكَ مَحَبَّةٌ عَظِيمَةٌ فَاصْبِرْ فَقَدْ بَلَغْتَ الْمُنَا
sentences.tr: fa-innahā ṣāra lahā fī qalbihā minka maḥabbatun ʿaẓīmatun fa-iṣbir fa-qad balaghta al-munā
sentences.l: For indeed-she, there has-become to-her in her-heart, from you, a great love; so be-patient, for you have reached the wishes.
sentences.i: For a great love for you has grown in her heart. Be patient: you have reached your wishes.
sentences.n: المنا is the edition's spelling of المنى (munā, plural of munya, "wish"), with alif for yā'; we point it as printed. The masculine صار before the feminine محبة is the usual agreement of a verb that precedes its subject.

sentences.t: فَصَبَرَ أَخِي وَطَاوَعَ الْجَارِيَةَ وَحَلَقَ ذَقْنَهُ وَأَخْرَجَتْهُ الصَّبِيَّةُ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣabara akhī wa-ṭāwaʿa al-jāriyata wa-ḥalaqa dhaqnahu wa-akhrajathu al-ṣabiyyatu
sentences.l: So my brother was-patient, and obeyed the girl, and shaved his chin, and the young-woman brought him out.
sentences.i: So my brother bore it, gave way to the maid, and had his beard shaved off; and the lady brought him out.
sentences.n: حلق has no stated agent. We read it as active (he had it done to himself); a passive ḥuliqa, "was shaved", is possible.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا هُوَ مَخْضُوبُ الْحَاجِبَيْنِ مَقْصُوصُ الشَّارِبَيْنِ مَحْلُوقُ الذَّقْنِ مُحْمَرُّ الْوَجْهِ فَفَزِعَتْ مِنْهُ ثُمَّ ضَحِكَتْ حَتَّى اسْتَلْقَتْ عَلَى قَفَاهَا ثُمَّ قَالَتْ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā huwa makhḍūbu al-ḥājibayni maqṣūṣu al-shāribayni maḥlūqu al-dhaqni muḥmarru al-wajhi fa-fazaʿat minhu thumma ḍaḥikat ḥattā istalqat ʿalā qafāhā thumma qālat
sentences.l: And behold, he (was) dyed-of the two eyebrows, clipped-of the two moustaches, shaved-of the chin, reddened-of the face; so she was-startled at him, then laughed until she lay-back upon her nape, then said:
sentences.i: And there he was: eyebrows dyed, moustache clipped, chin shaved, face glowing red. She started at the sight of him, then laughed until she fell on her back, and then said,
sentences.n: Each passive participle governs the following noun in the genitive, "dyed of the eyebrows" for "with dyed eyebrows". وَإِذَا هُوَ, "and behold, he", introduces the sudden sight.

sentences.t: يَا سَيِّدِي لَقَدْ مَلَكْتَنِي بِهَذِهِ الْأَخْلَاقِ الْحَسَنَةِ قَلْبِي
sentences.tr: yā sayyidī laqad malaktanī bi-hādhihi al-akhlāqi al-ḥasanati qalbī
sentences.l: O my master, you have indeed possessed me, by these good characters, my heart.
sentences.i: My lord, with these fine manners of yours you have taken possession of me, of my very heart.
sentences.n: قلبي stands loose at the end, as a second object or an afterthought: "you have taken me — my heart". The compliment is mockery; الأخلاق الحسنة are the "good qualities" she has just seen.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ حَلَّفَتْهُ بِحَيَاتِهَا أَنْ يَقُومَ وَيَرْقُصَ فَقَامَ وَرَقَصَ فَلَمْ تَدَعْ فِي الْبَيْتِ مِخَدَّةً حَتَّى ضَرَبَتْهُ بِهَا
sentences.tr: thumma ḥallafathu bi-ḥayātihā an yaqūma wa-yarquṣa fa-qāma wa-raqaṣa fa-lam tadaʿ fī al-bayti mikhaddatan ḥattā ḍarabathu bihā
sentences.l: Then she made-him-swear by her life that he rise and dance; so he rose and danced, and she did not leave in the house a cushion until she had struck him with it.
sentences.i: Then she made him swear by her life to get up and dance. He got up and danced, and she left not a cushion in the house without beating him with it.
sentences.n: The bi- of بِحَيَاتِهَا is the oath preposition ("by her life"). The print is unpointed, so ḥallafa (second form, "to administer an oath") is our reading.

sentences.t: وَكَذَلِكَ الْجَوَارِ كُلُّهُمْ صَارُوا يَضْرِبُونَهُ بِمِثْلِ نَارَنْجَةٍ وَلَيْمُونَةٍ وَ تُرُنْجَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-kadhālika al-jawāri kulluhum ṣārū yaḍribūnahu bi-mithli nāranjatin wa-laymūnatin wa-turunjatin
sentences.l: And likewise the maids, all-of-them, began they-beat-him with the like of a bitter-orange and a lemon and a citron,
sentences.i: And the other maids, every one of them, began to pelt him with the like of oranges, lemons and citrons,
sentences.n: صاروا is masculine plural with the feminine جوار, again; صار plus an imperfect means "began to". نارنجة, ليمونة and ترنجة are the bitter orange, the lemon and the citron. The print leaves a space after the conjunction in و ترنجة, as it does in several places below; kept.

sentences.t: إِلَى أَنْ سَقَطَ مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الضَّرْبِ وَ الصَّفْعِ عَلَى قَفَاهُ وَ الرَّجْمِ
sentences.tr: ilā an saqaṭa maghshiyyan ʿalayhi mina al-ḍarbi wa-al-ṣafʿi ʿalā qafāhu wa-al-rajmi
sentences.l: until he fell, covered-over upon him, from the beating and the slapping upon his nape and the stoning.
sentences.i: until he fell down in a faint from the blows, the slaps on his neck and the pelting.
sentences.n: الرجم is properly "stoning"; here it is the throwing of the fruit. Spaces after و are the print's.

sentences.t: فَقَلٰتْ لَهُ الْعَجُوزُ الْآنَ بَلَغْتَ مُرَادَكَ وَ اعْلَمْ أَنَّ مَا بَقِيَ عَلَيْكَ مِنَ الضَّرْبِ شَيٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu al-ʿajūzu al-āna balaghta murādaka wa-iʿlam anna mā baqiya ʿalayka mina al-ḍarbi shayʾun
sentences.l: So the old woman said to him: Now you have reached your aim; and know that there remains not upon you of the beating a thing,
sentences.i: Then the old woman said to him, "Now you have what you wanted. And know that nothing of the beating remains for you,
sentences.n: The print has فقلت, "I said", for فقالت, though the subject العجوز follows; it is a slip. We keep the letters and write the dagger alif that makes it read qālat. شيٌ is printed without its hamza; read shayʾun, with the edition's tanwīn.

sentences.t: وَمَا بَقِيَ إِلَّا شَيْأً وَاحِدًا وَ ذَلِكَ أَنَّ مِنْ عَادَتِنَا إِذَا سَكِرَتْ لَاتُمَكِّنُ أَحَدًا مِنْ نَفْسِهَا حَتَّى تَقْلَعَ ثِيَابَهَا وَ سَرَاوِيلَهَا وَ تَبْقَى عُرْيَانَةً زَلَطًا
sentences.tr: wa-mā baqiya illā shayʾan wāḥidan wa-dhālika anna min ʿādatinā idhā sakirat lātumakkinu aḥadan min nafsihā ḥattā taqlaʿa thiyābahā wa-sarāwīlahā wa-tabqā ʿuryānatan zalaṭan
sentences.l: and nothing remains but one thing; and that is that of our custom, when she gets drunk, she does not enable anyone of herself until she strips off her clothes and her trousers and remains naked, bare.
sentences.i: only one thing remains. It is our custom that when she is drunk she lets no one have her until she has stripped off her clothes and her drawers and stands stark naked,
sentences.n: The accusative شيأً after إِلَّا is Middle Arabic (classically nominative); the edition prints the أ and the tanwīn. لاتمكّن is one printed word, with the edition's shadda: مَكَّنَ مِنْ نَفْسِهَا, "to give access to herself", here sexual access. زلطا, "bare, stark", is a colloquial word and the vowelling is our guess.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَأْمُرُكَ بِقَلْعِ ثِيَابِكَ وَ تَجْرِي وَ هِيَ تَجْرِي قُدَّامَكَ كَأَنَّهَا هَارِبَةٌ مِنْكَ وَأَنْتَ تَابِعُهَا مِنْ مَكَانٍ إِلَى مَكَانٍ حَتَّى يَقُومَ أَيْرُكَ فَتُمَكِّنُكَ مِنْ نَفْسِهَا
sentences.tr: thumma taʾmuruka bi-qalʿi thiyābika wa-tajrī wa-hiya tajrī quddāmaka ka-annahā hāribatun minka wa-anta tābiʿuhā min makānin ilā makānin ḥattā yaqūma ayruka fa-tumakkinuka min nafsihā
sentences.l: Then she orders you to strip your clothes, and you run, and she runs in-front-of you as-if-she (were) fleeing from you, and you following her from place to place, until your cock stands; and she gives you access to herself.
sentences.i: Then she tells you to take off your clothes, and you run, and she runs ahead of you as though she were fleeing from you, and you chase her from place to place until your cock stands; and then she lets you have her.
sentences.n: The first تجري could be "you run" or "she runs"; we read "you run", then "she runs". قدامك is the spoken word for أمامك, "in front of you". أمر takes بِـ for the thing ordered. كَأَنَّهَا, "as if she", has كَـ in the sense of "like".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لَهُ اقْلَعْ ثِيَابَكَ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat lahu iqlaʿ thiyābaka
sentences.l: Then she said to him: Strip off your clothes.
sentences.i: Then she said to him, "Take off your clothes."

sentences.t: فَقَامَ وَ هُوَ غَائِبٌ عَنِ الْوُجُودِ وَقَلَعَ ثِيَابَهُ جَمِيعًا وَبَقِيَ عُرْيَانًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāma wa-huwa ghāʾibun ʿani al-wujūdi wa-qalaʿa thiyābahu jamīʿan wa-baqiya ʿuryānan
sentences.l: So he rose, and he (was) absent from existence, and stripped off his clothes, all-together, and remained naked.
sentences.i: He got up, half out of his senses, took off all his clothes, and stood there naked.
sentences.n: غائب عن الوجود, "absent from existence", is being out of one's wits; here it is the beating that has done it. The edition's precomposed ئ in غائب is kept.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ ال—ب—اح —
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿan al-kalāmi al-—b—āḥ —
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazad, and she fell silent from the speech al-[...]b[...]āḥ.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazad, and she fell silent, ceasing the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The closing formula of the night. The print is damaged at the end: ال—ب—اح with dashes is evidently الْمُبَاحِ, "the permitted", the usual rhyme with الصَّبَاحُ. The letters and dashes are left as printed and not pointed.
